# ADR 0093: Cron definition edits and original occurrence observations

- Date: 2026-10-24
- Status: Implementation candidate for the accepted Plan07 scope; focused qualification in progress.
- Owner: framework scheduler / original journal authority.

## Context and layering

`CronTaskStore` owns persisted definitions. `SchedulerRunner` owns the live
mutation permit, control/admission lock and callback settlement. Its existing
occurrence `DeliveryLedger` and file journal own event sequence, attempt and
terminal facts. EKO consumes this runner through its existing thin adapter.
Workspace IDs, TaskRun links, GUI grouping and application continuation policy
remain in EKO; the framework does not acquire them.

The original management API has no atomic definition edit. Removing and adding
changes the task identity and leaves a race. Returning only a callback string
also discards the occurrence/attempt and turns typed journal errors into text.
Finally, the old summary update treats a replaced definition as an execution
failure even after the original callback completed. These are different facts.

## References and options

The Plan07 investigation compared APScheduler's stable job ID plus reschedule
model and Kubernetes resource-version conflict rejection:

- https://apscheduler.readthedocs.io/en/3.x/userguide.html#modifying-jobs
- https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/api-concepts/

We use the existing definition generation as the CAS token, keeping the original
store and runner. We do not import another scheduler, a distributed authority,
remove/add editing, or application retry policy. Tokio's owned tasks keep the
original operation alive when only its observer disappears:
https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/task/struct.JoinHandle.html

A second execution queue or history store would create competing facts. Parsing
a callback's output to discover an application run would invent a contract.
Instead, all three public observations extend the current owner paths.

## Decision

`CronTaskEdit` contains only name, cron expression and prompt.
`SchedulerRunner::edit_task(expected, edit)` enters the existing owned mutation
and control lock, then the store mutation lock. The store checks only the
expected ID and `same_definition`: nonempty definition ID, or both legacy IDs
empty and equal creation timestamps. Other expected fields never overwrite the
latest status, control revision or summary.

An actual edit preserves task ID, creation timestamp and current status, assigns
a new definition ID, checked-increments the control revision, and clears the new
definition's last-run summary. A no-op returns the exact current snapshot without
writing. Invalid cron, missing/conflicting definition, exhausted revision,
closed runner, unavailable authority, no-commit and unknown-commit are explicit
errors. Unknown writes retain the original store poison; no edit is retried by
this API. Standalone `CronTaskStore::edit` obeys the existing runner permit.

The old admission check rejects an old definition/control token that has not
started its effect. An already `EffectStarted` callback keeps its captured
snapshot and owner. Replaced/deleted definitions yield `Superseded` only for
summary projection: no write and no stale cache insertion. Real I/O or poison is
still a projection error. The original occurrence result is never reassigned.
The derived scheduled watermark drops an old definition cache key when its new
definition is first admitted, without deleting journal facts.

`run_once_with_receipt` is the original manual admit/drain/callback-completion
path. `run_once` only maps its result and error for existing callers. A successful
receipt includes the captured task/definition/occurrence/time/trigger, exact
attempt and unparsed callback string, plus the original terminal `ApplyReceipt`.
The original append receipt may record degraded append durability when a later
original durability barrier succeeded; success requires that barrier too.

Errors retain known occurrence/attempt facts, including the original claim when
its commit or durability observation fails, actual callback observations,
projection errors and the original typed journal cause. Journal failure metadata
keeps NotCommitted/Committed/Unknown, batch identity, the original single/batch
receipt when one exists, and the original retry/reopen flags. A reopen flag is
absent when the original error does not supply a typed requirement, rather than
guessing a recovery policy from its text. These flags describe
the retained journal operation, not permission to start another manual request.
Physical `ExecutionNotSettled`, callback failure, projection failure and terminal
commit failure remain distinct. No output string is parsed and no application
run ID is added. Dropping an observer does not cancel the admitted callback owner.

`read_occurrence_history(cursor, limit)` returns original typed delivery events,
projecting only the private captured payload into `SchedulerOccurrenceSnapshot`.
It preserves metadata, sequence and physical batch ID. The cursor binds journal
generation, retained floor, initial snapshot upper sequence and continuation.
The default is 128 events; explicit limits must be 1 through 512. These are
resource policy bounds, not measured performance thresholds. Every page reuses
indexed bounded `replay_after`; scheduler writes use single-record frames or the
existing two-record recovery admission batch. No full-tail read, claim,
checkpoint/recovery, callback or history write occurs. An exhausted old snapshot
does not absorb newly appended events. Missing/corrupt sequences, wrong
generation/floor, invalid cursors and unavailable journals fail explicitly.
The hot projection's terminal retention is not complete history.

## File journal poison and recovery boundary

Tracked framework and EKO callers and existing fault tests were inspected.
EKO chat-log replay uses the separate segmented journal; event-bus replay is a
different API. `CheckpointedReducer::recover` already propagates journal read
errors. Existing file-journal unknown-commit tests drop the poisoned authority
before verified reopen. No current contract promising a trusted page from a
live poisoned file handle was found. A confirmed full-write degraded receipt or
retryable `sync_data` failure does not by itself poison the journal and remains
readable.

For nonzero reads the original file `replay_after` now checks poison under its
existing state lock before returning any page, including an otherwise empty
page. This is an observable read precondition: unknown commit requires the
original close/reopen/recovery and retained-batch lookup before trusted history.
The original error propagates; it is never translated into an empty page, new
generation or reset cursor. There is no second reader/validator/store and no new
recovery or retry policy. Zero-limit no-read behavior of the generic journal is
unchanged; the scheduler rejects zero limits itself.

## Validation and delivery

Regression definitions cover stale/no-op/legacy/invalid/exhausted edits, runner
permit and ambiguous writes; old unstarted and already-started occurrences;
independent manual identities and legacy mapping; callback/unsettled/projection/
terminal boundaries; snapshot/cursor/limit behavior and absence of read effects.
An after-claim-commit observation fault checks ordinary/manual and legacy
recovery batch paths against their actual committed claim and receipt, without
starting a callback. This control does not simulate a physical sync failure.
The journal fault case injects an actual unknown full append, rejects the live
page, then reopens and reads the original committed facts. Known degraded reads
keep their existing controls.

Two controlled restorations of prior behavior produced actual failing
assertions: a completed callback lost success after definition replacement, and
a poisoned file journal returned a trusted history page. These controls changed
only the original behavior branches in the candidate; they were not a build of
the whole earlier revision. The corresponding candidate controls preserve
terminal completion, untouched replacement summary and no-replay checks.

The candidate scheduler suite passed 82 tests and the journal suite passed 117,
with zero failures or ignored tests; the example check passed without warnings.
Focused lint gates are also required before a local implementation checkpoint.
This is focused evidence only. Full-gate, integrated consumer, native GUI and
external-service acceptance remain pending.
The existing `demo70_scheduler` example remains in the learning crate's executable
all-targets chain and must compile with the qualified framework. Documentation
is updated in both long-running-task chapters; the facade already re-exports the
scheduler module. No manifest, lock, shared README or root library changes are
needed. Website mirrors belong to the integration owner after qualified source
delivery. This adds no accepted SDK wire/route/member automatically.

Source: https://echo-agent.dev/docs/adr-0094-subagent-tool-boundary-inheritance

# ADR 0094: Invocation Tool Scope Across Subagent Dispatch

## Status

Implementation candidate. Hard-tool-scope and the separate target-policy
increment passed source review and their focused Rust checks. Full matrix and
consumer delivery remain pending.

## Context

The framework already has one tool registry, invocation disabled tools and
`ToolVisibilityState` with available, eligible and visible sets. A parent can
exclude tools for one task without removing them from a shared Agent or role.
That hard bound must survive a subsequent dispatch to a fresh or differently
configured Subagent.

`ParentContextFactory` builds transferable history and definitions, while
`SubagentContext.allowed_tools` carries a nonempty invocation whitelist. The
old dispatch factory did not populate that whitelist. Fork applied an existing
disabled mask, but did not construct invocation visibility for the next child.
Sync and Teammate omitted the mask altogether. Team discarded scope-only
parent contexts when they had no history or goal. A prompt-only capability
projection could therefore describe a restriction that actual execution lost.

This is a generic framework defect. Applications own their role selection,
depth defaults, configuration and run binding. This change does not impose an
application's maximum depth or introduce new policy storage.

## Reference implementations

The accepted design investigation consulted Claude Code's
[Subagent tool restrictions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents) and
the OpenAI Agents SDK's
[manager and agent-as-tool composition](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/multi_agent/).
Those references separate a child invocation's capabilities from its prompt
and conversation context. Here the existing invocation mask and dispatch
context provide that boundary; another executor or permission service would
duplicate it.

## Options

1. Filter only the inherited prompt/tool descriptions. Rejected because direct
   or stale model calls could still execute a registered tool.
2. Copy the shared tool manager or the first-turn visible set. Rejected because
   the shared catalog is wider than task authority, while deferred tools may
   legitimately be available without being visible yet.
3. Reuse the original available set, `allowed_tools`, invocation and
   execution pipeline. Selected because all modes retain one authority.

## Decision

`AgentDispatchTool` snapshots `ToolContext.tool_visibility.available_names()`
when the invoking context supplies it. This is the immutable available catalog,
not the mutable eligible/visible subset. A cached direct dispatch whose hard
scope excludes `agent_tool` fails before creating a child. An absent visibility
context keeps the original standalone framework behavior.

The original `SubagentContext` carries the known nonempty bound independently
of transcript inheritance, including Fresh mode and calls without a history
factory. Its private merge intersects an existing nonempty bound, rejects an
empty intersection without mutation, and never converts that result into the
historical unrestricted `Some([])` spelling. Shared parent definitions are
only descriptive context and do not grant missing authority.

All concrete Sync, Fork and Teammate invocations carry the original nonempty
set in `AgentInvocationContext.allowed_tools: Option<HashSet<String>>`.
An exclusion list computed before admission cannot express tools registered
while the shared Agent waits for its execution lock. The original snapshot
therefore intersects the then-current catalog with the positive bound after
that lock is acquired. Initial visible schemas remain a separate subset;
omitting them exposes the eligible part of the bounded catalog. A nonempty
bound matching no current tools remains nonempty until this intersection.

This extends the original invocation carrier rather than adding another
permission state. The original available/eligible/visible authority in the
child governs model requests, tool search and execution, so a later dispatch
retains its hard available bound. Team preserves a context
containing only a tool scope and passes it through the existing member dispatch.
The original tool search and execution pipeline apply the same mask; promoting
eligibility cannot add names outside the available set.

`None` and an empty set/list in either `allowed_tools` carrier mean no
additional whitelist. A nonempty bound that matches no tool in a new role
still disables every concrete role tool. It is never rewritten as an empty
declaration that would restore the whole registry. Existing model, skill,
read-only, cancellation, exact-attempt and delegation policies can narrow the
result further and retain their original owners.

## Consequences

- The public Rust invocation structure gains one optional field. Exhaustive
  struct literals must provide it or use the original Default update syntax.
  The existing `ToolRuntime::from_agent` public signature stays unchanged.
  No store, validator, executor, dependency or external wire contract is added.
- A constrained Sync or Teammate dispatch now enforces its already-declared
  whitelist in actual model requests and tool execution, as Fork does.
- A child may use tools its parent deferred from the initial visible set if
  those tools are within the inherited hard available bound and its own role.
- Independent callers with no whitelist remain unchanged. Applications must
  supply trustworthy invocation bounds; missing application run bindings are
  not synthesized by this generic repair.
- Framework nested delegation defaults and consumer-selected maximums remain
  independent. This ADR does not implement any GUI depth setting, TaskRun
  persistence or SDK accepted contract.
- EKO exhaustive literals are adapted by the application owner. The separately
  pinned SDK's inspected literals use Default and need no mechanical field
  addition; a future pin still requires its own verification. Full Rust public
  inventory is telemetry and does not automatically add accepted SDK members.

## Verification and rollback

Test definitions use actual `LlmClient` requests and forced out-of-scope tool
calls across Sync, Fork, Teammate and Team, including zero role matches. They
also cover a nested Fresh factory dispatch to a new role, cached direct
dispatch, hard-set intersection, legacy empty/absent scopes and tool-search
promotion. A deterministic queued-turn control holds the real ReactAgent
execution mutex, observes the original invocation before queue admission,
registers a previously absent tool through the shared Agent, releases the
lock, then checks actual model requests/search and the forced tool side effect.
It covers all four modes through concrete original member dispatch.

Two controlled restorations of prior behavior compiled and failed their selected
assertions: one lost the ancestor scope, and one let a tool registered during
queueing enter later model requests. The new field's structure remained present;
these were narrow semantic controls, not builds of the whole previous revision.
Compilation failure or a missing API does not count as a behavioral counterexample.

Focused `subagent` feature validation passed 22 dispatch, 196 Subagent and 26
snapshot tests: 244 selected, zero failures or ignored tests. All nine new tests
ran. The changed `demo61_agent_factory` compiled under its existing `testing`
feature, and the unchanged communication demo50 compiled under `subagent`.
Focused library/test Clippy and demo61 Clippy passed without warnings.

These results qualify the framework contribution's focused paths. The complete
feature matrix, EKO configuration/run binding and GUI, independent SDK consumer,
native/service behavior and precise main CI still require their own acceptance.
Logs and source identities remain outside the build target; the owned target
was cleaned after the granted Rust batch.

Rollback is a normal source revert. No persisted schema or run record changes.
Reverting restores the old scope-propagation defect and must not be presented
as equivalent enforcement.

## Exact actor policy at the original invocation boundary

Source follow-up found two independent gaps not qualified by the 244 hard-scope
tests above. Sync and Teammate copied a parent's runtime policy while the
request already contained the target child's policy; an actual child could
therefore report the parent depth to its own tools. Snapshot also constructed
tool qualification before selecting the effective policy. An exhausted or
explicitly nondelegating actor could still advertise `agent_tool`, and absent
visibility let tool search read the wider registry.

The existing executor invocation helper now copies the request's target policy
into the original `ExternalRunContext`, creating that carrier when absent.
It does not call `child_policy` or add a level. The original actual dispatch
edge remains the single increment; correct Fork/exact/Team-member target
identities retain their existing values. No product depth constant is added.

Snapshot selects the effective policy once, using its original precedence:
an explicit invocation, including one with no policy, does not fall back to
legacy state. That same value feeds both ToolContext and original ToolRuntime.
An explicit `can_delegate() == false` removes `agent_tool` through the existing
disabled/available/eligible authority and establishes that authority even when
initial visibility is absent. Thus schema, search and forced calls share one
qualification. Policy `None` preserves the original framework behavior. A hard
scope containing only `agent_tool` intersected with a nondelegating policy
remains an empty available catalog, never an unrestricted fallback.
When policy alone requires this qualification, initial schemas retain the
original NoDeferred surface and keep `tool_search` hidden. Explicit deferred
visibility and hard-scope invocations retain their existing search behavior;
direct searches still consume the same qualified available/eligible catalog.

New regression definitions observe actual child ToolContext and model requests
for Sync/Fork/Teammate at maximums 1/2/3 and an independent generic maximum 4,
the original Team coordinator/member edge, explicit primary and legacy policy,
invocation precedence, search and forced stale dispatch with no new start event.
The separate target-policy batch selected all five new definitions and passed
249 distinct tests: 25 dispatch, 196 Subagent and 28 snapshot tests, with zero
failures, ignored tests or compiler warnings. Both existing examples compiled
with their actual features, and focused library/test Clippy passed. Two narrow
restorations of prior behavior each compiled and failed one selected assertion:
the child reported parent depth, and primary model schemas exposed delegation
under an explicit nondelegating policy. The first attempt instead failed to
compile because two new tests matched an Arc event as its enum; no test ran,
and that output is retained separately from behavioral red evidence.

This is a focused framework contribution. It does not qualify the full feature
matrix, EKO GUI persistence, run/recovery binding, role catalog or SDK contracts.
Raw results and exact target cleanup are recorded in
`evidence.subagent-depth-target-policy`; the earlier 244-test hard-scope evidence
remains a separate historical checkpoint.

## 程序化委派桥的完整目标策略

后续源码核对确认，带 runtime context 的 text/message 程序化 delegate helper
曾把调用方已经提供的完整目标 policy 重建为 legacy `policy_from_depth`，导致
Fork 再次覆盖目标上下文中的最大层数与可委派资格。应用冻结的 1/2 上限因此可能
被改成 3。该缺陷属于通用值传递，不应由应用重写调度器或逐工具查询配置修补。

两种 helper 的私有 inner 共用完整策略解析：显式 runtime policy 原样保留三字段，
同时核对原 `depth` 参数指向同一目标层数；冲突在选择/构造目标 Agent 前明确拒绝。
没有完整 policy 的旧调用继续原 legacy 转换。这里不调用 `child_policy`，不增加
public API，也不改变独立复用方的上限、原 exact attempt、取消或 Fork 结算 owner。
应用只负责提供自己原 TaskRun/turn 已冻结的策略。

回归通过真实 ReactAgent/Fork、原 `agent_tool` 和实际 ToolContext 观察，不以提示词
或伪 dispatcher 比字段代替。源码定义与 focused 执行、应用/GUI/main 资格分别记录，
不把本节说明当成尚未取得的完整矩阵或原生验收。

## 2026-10-27：调用级只读能力与受限委派

### 背景与候选

真实只读 reviewer 已声明可委派，但普通 `agent_tool` 的 Mutating 能力被原只读快照正确过滤，合法下一层因此不可达。仅把全部 dispatcher 标成 ReadOnly 会扩大普通 writer 的能力；仅核目标角色标签又无法防止错误只读标签的 Agent 实际装入写工具。二者均不采用。

采用原 `ToolAccess` 的可选调用上界，沿 `AgentInvocationContext`、`ToolContext`、`SubagentContext` 三个既有载体传递。它不形成新的权限 store、角色策略或任务状态。`None` 保留旧调用，任何已有 ReadOnly 均不得被 Mutating 值提升；Fresh、空历史及没有 Goal 时仍保留 access-only context。

### 决策与数据流

只读 Agent 的原装配选择 `AgentDispatchTool::read_only`，普通 `new` 继续声明 Mutating；受限实例的 capabilities.access 为 ReadOnly，模型 catalog 只列只读目标；运行 risk 保留 Standard，沿原 `tool_search` 的分类方式避免结果缓存。调用必须具备原 `ToolContext` 的有效 visibility，从不可变 available 集继承父工具上界；缺上下文、缺范围或空交集明确失败，不回退无限制。此检查防本地运行时丢失约束后误写用户文件，不限制用户直接打开终端或配置 MCP，也不要求 full-auto。

同一不可变 registration 在 factory 前合并目标自身的 ReadOnly 声明与祖先上界，再验证只读调用不得选择 writer。目标声明是已有 typed mutation boundary，普通 writer 父或 None 调用也不能让被标为 ReadOnly 的目标误执行写工具；这个上界保留在原请求中，失败后的重试/转派不能降权。后续执行仍用该 record；Team 的实际成员/manager 同样逐项进入原准入，不按外层 Team 标签放行写成员。Sync、Fork、Teammate、Team 与后台沿原执行器传递同一调用值，不另建调度或改变取消、物理结算与深度计数。

Agent 获得原执行锁后，`ToolRuntime` 从当前 catalog 计算配置只读与调用 ReadOnly 的有效值。模型 schema、tool_search 可用集及最终工具执行共同沿该快照过滤，再与父工具正向集合、disabled/model/skill/depth 条件求交；同名替换或排队后注册写工具不能扩大权限。`ToolRuntime::from_agent` 仍保原公开签名；只有内部构造接受调用上界。默认 `Agent` 三个 invocation 回退不能落实 ReadOnly，因此在旧 execute/chat 开始前明确返回不支持，None 正控制不变；ReactAgent 和 Arc 转发承接完整上下文。

### 影响与验收

追加公开 Rust 字段要求使用完整 struct literal 的调用方明确补值，使用 Default 的原代码无需机械改写；不宣称完全源码兼容，不自动升级 SDK pin/accepted 或把完整 public inventory 当跨语言承诺。Framework 保留合理 max4/None/writer 消费能力；EKO 的默认总层数1、GUI最多3及真实 reviewer 工厂资格归应用。

要求真实旧只读 schema/工厂行为先红后绿，验证四模式/后台、Fresh/access-only、同一 record、writer/错误标签/Team混写、工具搜索/强制调用/晚注册/同名替换及默认回退负控制。执行层数、公开字段 literal 与示例需适用编译；原生、完整 feature/工程矩阵、精确 main/CI 和 SDK 独立来源分别验收，定向通过不替代它们。官方参考沿本 ADR 与跨仓已审设计的原件，不把注册表 `tool_names()` 当实际模型曝光证据。

### 安全收口补充：只读能力不等于派发结果可缓存

`ToolAccess::ReadOnly` 约束后代不得改写用户环境；派发本身仍建立新的子调用生命周期与真实回执。原 ToolManager 以 `ToolRiskLevel::ReadOnly` 进入成功结果缓存，其上下文键不包含每个独立 call_id，因此不能把受限派发也按普通可缓存读取分类。这里复用原 tool_search 的既有模式：普通和受限 dispatcher 的运行 risk 均为 Standard，只有受限实例的 capability access 为 ReadOnly。只读 schema、搜索和最终准入继续检查 access，不依赖缓存分类。

没有新增 cache trait、工具名特例或全局缓存策略；两次相同参数但独立 call_id 的合法派发必须实际建立两次子调用，不重放旧结果或旧“已启动”回执。该回归经原 ToolManager 实际入口取得一次实际调用/预期两次的行为失败，再验证修复；这项局部修复不代表当前只读整体、原生或后继原生 reasoning/assistant 执行切换已经完成。

# ADR 0095: Structured remote Tool failures

## Status and scope

Accepted implementation direction; source implementation and actual Rust/SDK
qualification are pending. Date: 2026-10-25.

The project coordinator selected this technical direction within the authorized
tool-governance Goal. It does not accept a new SDK value, change the SDK's pinned
framework revision, or authorize publication. The stage design is the workspace
`docs/supreme/specs/tool-failure-classification/design.md` (SHA-256
`2396bd58ae3f66a66ae5decc7ba649d5c7081243cc49320f2c53a9e67e26163c`);
the precise implementation source is Plan `8a4ad068-ab49-43c3-b29d-92bbd0b8a6c7`
at workspace checkpoint `b47ef77223f59c9ab9e98888fd317e4fd75535a8`.

## Context

Search providers return the existing `Result<Vec<SearchResult>, ReactError>`.
They currently erase HTTP/transport facts into `ToolError::ExecutionFailed`
messages; WebSearchTool then labels every provider failure Transient/Retry with
a fabricated one-second hint. Authentication, quota, malformed responses and
network failures therefore cannot retain their actual recovery contracts.

ToolFailure already owns category, recovery, side effects, retry_after_ms,
idempotency and postconditions. ToolManager already owns retries, permits,
admission, cancellable waiting and started/draining settlement. Neither is
replaced. ToolFailure does not contain tool identity or a display message.

## Decision

Add `ToolError::RemoteFailure` with `tool: String`, `message: String`,
`http_status: Option<u16>` and `failure: Box<ToolFailure>`. Tool/message each
have one owner; the existing ToolFailure owns recovery facts. The box contains
the additional payload without putting reqwest types in echo-core. Existing
ExecutionFailed/Timeout/Cancelled and SearchProvider signatures stay intact.

Providers and their original body-reading boundaries classify facts while the
HTTP status, headers or typed reqwest error still exist. Core receives ordinary
values. `ToolFailure::from_error` retains the structured payload and can only
narrow recovery for the caller's side-effect scope; Possible/Confirmed effects
are never downgraded and idempotency is never invented. The original AgentFailure
projection keeps Tool domain, terminal cause and optional HTTP status.

WebSearchTool preserves the resulting typed failure instead of overriding it.
Timeout and cancellation use existing error variants. Unclassified legacy
ExecutionFailed remains subject to the original conservative classification;
neither exception text nor provider names determine retryability.

### Classification

- Existing pre-request query/limit/cursor-type checks retain InvalidArguments;
  nonempty cursor decoding/version/fingerprint/offset checks remain after the
  original fetch in paginate. No cursor validator or cache is added.
- Invalid endpoint/request construction, HTTP401/402/403/404 and other permanent
  client failures stop. HTTP408 is Timeout; HTTP429 and HTTP500..599 are Transient.
  Known timeout/connection causes retain their typed classification. Original
  content/decoding failures stop; original size-limit errors retain their type.
- Cancellation/interruptions are Cancelled; ExecutionNotSettled stays an
  observation, not a terminal failure or permission to repeat physical work.
- Diagnostics exclude credentials, raw error bodies and sensitive URL details.

DDG retains its existing successful-HTML anti-bot/empty-results fallback to the
Instant Answer API. One provider/manager logical attempt can therefore perform
one or two original HTTP sends. Strategy fallback and manager failure retry are
counted separately. DDG retains reqwest text/json decoding and body-size behavior;
shared readers retain their own limits. Body-size governance is a separate task.

### Retry hints and lifecycle

Normalize valid Retry-After seconds or HTTP-date to the existing retry_after_ms.
Missing/malformed hints stay None; valid zero/past dates are Some(0). HTTP-date
parsing reuses a mature parser; a direct dependency must be declared and checked
even if its package already exists transitively in Cargo.lock.

ToolManager remains the only retry executor for typed results and Err paths.
Both retain the hint, retry count, admission, cancellation, side-effect policy,
stream-output replay restrictions and original drain owner. Keep the existing
30-second maximum delay: when the server minimum cannot fit it, return the
original typed failure instead of retrying early. No scheduler or queue is added.

## Alternatives and external references

Adding optional fields to existing ExecutionFailed would change accepted field
shapes and every existing constructor. Parsing error strings loses facts and
does not solve classification. Borrowing LLM/Channel errors misstates ownership.
All are rejected in favor of one additional carrier using ToolFailure.

Official [reqwest Error](https://docs.rs/reqwest/0.12.28/reqwest/struct.Error.html)
retains typed timeout/connect/status facts and supports stripping URLs;
[Response](https://docs.rs/reqwest/0.12.28/reqwest/struct.Response.html) exposes
status/headers before body consumption. Smithy's
[ProvideErrorKind](https://docs.rs/aws-smithy-types/latest/aws_smithy_types/retry/trait.ProvideErrorKind.html)
separates optional retry facts from display text. This framework reuses its
existing failure taxonomy and execution owner rather than importing another one.

## Consequences

Rust consumers that exhaustively match ToolError must handle the added variant;
existing constructors and provider trait signatures do not change. HTTP facts
become available to the existing recovery and adapter paths without another
network dependency in core. Public inventory changes must be distinguished from
explicitly accepted SDK identities. Source review alone does not qualify this
change or remove the original effect/settlement obligations.

## SDK, documentation and validation

ToolError is already in the SDK accepted contract. A new Rust variant and its
fields do not automatically become accepted source identities. The existing
collector records variant/field identities separately and removes structural
child IDs from retained signatures; only actual candidate collection can prove
the complete retained contract. The existing ToolFailureWire/AgentFailureWire
can project failure facts without assuming new wire fields or a protocol bump.
The current SDK pin and language acceptance stay unchanged until separately
qualified. Static inspection is not 5352-item/431-route byte parity.

Before/after regression must exercise real provider/Tool/manager behavior and
count logical attempts and endpoint HTTP sends. Cover statuses, valid/invalid
Retry-After, cancellation, content errors, original DDG fallback, cursor rejection
and successful pagination; also cover Err/typed-result side effects and both
ReAct and a Host built from the actual candidate. Old-pinned Host tests cannot
qualify the new source. Public API/feature/dependency gates and examples remain
required. This ADR does not claim any such run has occurred.

Exa's independent4343 commit is unchanged and unmerged. The separate P1-A output
budget source and original evidence remain preserved; sharing a final validation
batch does not merge their acceptance claims or create a completed old contract.

# ADR 0096: Selective prepared plugin content identities

## Status

Accepted for implementation. This source contribution is not yet Rust-qualified or delivered to main.

## Context

ADR 0012 owns a same-read immutable plugin generation, original registry dependency validation,
and per-Agent publication/cleanup. Its whole-set identity changes when any member changes.
An embedding application needs the content identities of a selected plugin and its real declared
closure without treating every installed plugin, a version label, or a process ordinal as that
selection's content identity. Optional manifest versions must retain their original meaning.

The approved task-bound domain design assigns this reusable mechanism to the framework and
product rule parsing/admission to the application. It does not authorize a second manager,
validator, version archive or resource owner. ADR 0012's Codex/Claude reload references provide
the existing immutable-preparation rationale; the application design's Temporal/LangGraph
comparison motivates detecting content drift rather than silently reinterpreting persisted work.

## Alternatives

- Use whole-set identity: rejects unaffected work when an unrelated plugin changes.
- Use name/version or generation: misses same-version edits or changes after process restart.
- Rescan files/resolve dependencies in each consumer: creates competing input and validation authorities.
- Archive complete old packages/resources: outside this mechanism and not provided by holding an Arc.

## Decision

Add `PreparedPlugin::content_identity()` and
`PreparedPluginSet::dependency_closure(plugin_id)` to the existing facade. Original prepare
builds each identity from the same manifest/configuration and frozen documents that it publishes.
Canonical JSON object keys and manifest dependency order prevent HashMap/insertion-order drift;
array order otherwise remains meaningful. The original variable substitution also orders its existing
user-config pass by key, so references inside values cannot change frozen text with HashMap order.
Built-in → user-config → environment stages remain unchanged; this adds no recursive expansion
or new variable resolver. Identity normalization never hides differing published instructions.
Documents include their component kind, relative source
and bytes, using the existing length-delimited hash framing. Each plugin keeps its validated
outgoing dependency names; selection only walks that frozen graph and filters the original stable
dependency-first sequence. Original registry checks remain the sole presence/enabled/version/cycle
validator. Invalid generations and missing roots cannot return a usable closure.

Whole-set identity continues to describe complete publication, aggregating all canonical plugin
identities. This changes its digest encoding, not its owner or admission responsibilities; previous
strings are not persistent cross-version API versions. Publication targets and issued receipt
checks remain untouched. Single-plugin identity excludes dependency contents so consumers can
retain each real provider identity; the returned closure supplies transitive dependencies explicitly.

Coverage is limited to the original framework's prepared inputs, including discovered Skill identity
documents, Hook/MCP declarations and frozen Subagent documents. Existing frozen adapter inputs
continue their original feature handling until their separately approved retirement is integrated.
The mechanism does not freeze unread helper scripts, complete references directories, external
commands/services, model results or physical side effects. It contains no EKO policy or credentials
projection. Applications retain responsibility for their own same-read components and actual
invocation admission; an old prepared Arc is observation, not authority to use retired resources.

## Consequences and validation

Extend the existing plugin example instead of adding a new demo count/target. Retain existing
publication, stale generation, cancellation, rollback and cleanup tests. Add selection controls
for transitive changes versus unrelated changes, stable reprepare/restart and dependency order,
absent versions, original dependency refusals, nested object order and unread Skill helper boundaries.
Docs in both languages describe the coverage and the aggregate encoding change.

This source phase runs no Cargo, rustfmt, metadata or native process and creates no target.
Focused Rust/example qualification and any applicable feature/full gates run only in the
coordinator's resource window; logs must be retained outside the precise target before its guarded
cargo clean. SDK pin/accepted contracts and website publication are not changed by this contribution.

## References

- [ADR 0012](0012-immutable-plugin-preparation.md)
- [ADR 0069](0069-plugin-host-lifecycle-coordinator.md)
- Cross-repository approved design: `eko-domain-plugin-runtime/design.md`, sections 3, 5, 7, 10 and 12.

Source: https://echo-agent.dev/docs/adr-0097-subagent-registration-admission

# ADR 0097: Admit and Consume One Subagent Registration

## Status

Implementation candidate with focused Subagent qualification. The selected
runtime controls, public callback example and relevant lint checks passed;
full workspace/features, consumer qualification and exact main CI remain
separate. No SDK accepted surface or consumer pin changes here.

## Context

`SubagentRegistry` already owns atomic records containing a definition, a lazy
factory or pre-built Agent, an original `OnceCell`, and a revision. Its lazy
cache publication already fences replaced revisions. Dispatch nevertheless
looked up definition and executable separately by name. A valid concurrent
registration/removal could change the factory, timeout, inheritance or Team
member after a caller inspected the definition.

Lifecycle `SubagentHooks::before_dispatch` returns `()`. It observes a dispatch;
it cannot veto one. Outer tool checks and prompt compilation cannot establish
that the subsequently selected factory belongs to the checked definition.
Hosts need a product-neutral check on the actual selected object before any
user factory, model or background child starts. This local correctness check
prevents framework concurrency from substituting an unvalidated object; it
does not add a permission mode, GUI gate or HITL flow.

## Reference implementations

The confirmed design investigation used the OpenAI Agents SDK's
[tool execution](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/0dc4cf152bff1f50bdc0e41f28808563406545b2/src/agents/run_internal/tool_execution.py#L2021):
the selected `FunctionTool` is used both by input checks and by invocation.
Its [lifecycle hooks](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/0dc4cf152bff1f50bdc0e41f28808563406545b2/src/agents/lifecycle.py#L83)
are a separate observation mechanism. The
[Claude Agent SDK hook types](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/0e89b298e771259378a6cd3734e00d323dff5703/src/claude_agent_sdk/types.py#L511)
also distinguish pre-tool execution control from Subagent-start context
contributions. This change follows the shared selected-object pattern;
these references do not qualify Rust execution or application resource leases.

## Options

1. Recheck a name in an outer tool or observation hook. Rejected: a later
   factory lookup can select another record, and observation is not refusal.
2. Disable all dynamic registration while a host uses Subagents. Rejected:
   this removes legitimate framework/General self-extension and does not
   express the actual host execution contract.
3. Select and admit the original registry record, then consume its paired
   executable through the original dispatcher. Selected: no new registry,
   executor, store, retry loop, dependency or resource owner is required.

## Decision

`resolve_registration` snapshots one record into `SubagentRegistration` without
calling a factory. The handle retains the original factory/cache cell and an
opaque weak reference to the owning registry state. Public accessors expose
the actual definition, factory/instance availability and diagnostic revision.
`is_same_registration` compares registry and original record identity. The
revision is process-local and must never become a persisted plugin version.

An optional `SubagentRegistrationAdmission` is configured on the original
registry. All its executors, including existing Agent-created dispatchers,
share that configuration. `admit` receives the selected record and the
original `DispatchRequest`, including `runtime_context`, run identity and
existing invocation guards. The framework checks registry/target ownership
first, clones the callback under its configuration lock, then releases all
registry/configuration locks before awaiting host code or invoking a factory.
Hosts own their provider/content/run interpretation. No EKO field enters the
generic API. A policy must not retain strong references back to its long-lived
Agent/registry or keep invocation resources beyond its own scoped ownership.

`agent_tool` resolves once for isolation/mode/background routing and passes
that same handle to the original registered dispatch entry. Sync, Fork,
Teammate and Team root/member selection consume the admitted record. Every
retry or transfer to a new target resolves and admits its actual record anew.
Fresh factory instances still take precedence over a cached instance, and
dispatch never publishes a fresh result into another registration's cell.
The original public lazy-cache lookup and its singleflight/publication fences
remain unchanged; they are raw construction APIs, not policy-bearing dispatch.

Background admission happens before the spawn/handle return. Its admitted
first record is consumed once, without a second policy call in the spawned
owner; later retries are checked anew. A refused controlled-background attempt
settles its original reservation without creating an Agent. Existing exact
attempt, cancellation, tool scope, depth, isolation, physical-settlement and
invocation-guard authorities remain in place.

The explicit public `dispatch_teammate().join()` entry also reuses the original
non-process keyed resource bundle. Only that direct entry transfers this
bundle to the already-existing Teammate physical task; `dispatch_inner` keeps
its own original bundle and does not allocate another one. Stream-setup
`ExecutionNotSettled` can occur before the Agent default wrapper constructs a
retaining stream, so a context/handle alone cannot retain the last guard.
Unknown settlement or unwind transfers it to the same original keyed debt
owner; known original EOF releases it. Dropping a handle requests cancellation
and does not abort that original physical task or release its guards early.

Team members receive the original parent invocation's real guard clones in
their original runtime context. The retained Team dispatch closure holds only
a weak reference to that invocation-scoped bundle; actual dispatch must
upgrade it while the original call is alive, before policy/factory consumption.
An expired guarded source refuses new members. This avoids a completed,
retained runtime handle indefinitely holding the old pool lease. Calls that
never supplied guards keep their original behavior. This is propagation of
the existing guard carrier, not another lease/slot/cleanup authority.

A same-name replacement or removal affects future selections. An already
admitted invocation may finish with the original record; it never silently
switches to the replacement. Passing a handle from another registry, even
with the same name/revision, is refused. Configuring a new callback affects
subsequent admissions and does not revoke already admitted in-flight work.
Consumers needing atomic product publication continue to use their original
generation/lease owner; this handle is not a frozen historical environment.

## Consequences

- No callback means the original dynamic-registration/fresh-dispatch behavior.
- Existing by-name executor APIs now take the same checked record path.
- Host refusal precedes user factories and actual child execution. It is
  returned through the existing error channel, not a new runtime state.
- Public Rust additions require normal feature/API verification. They do not
  automatically become language SDK accepted contracts or update its pin.
- The communication example demonstrates admission with original attempt
  identity. The public Subagent guides and website mirror need to stay aligned.

## Verification and rollback

Regression definitions run actual executor, agent_tool and Team paths. Held
semaphores interleave policy checks or factory construction with registration
replacement/removal. They check exact definition/executable pairing, refusal
before zero factory calls, no stale result in the replacement's lazy cache,
foreign-registry handles, cancellation during policy wait, fresh retry/retarget
checks, controlled-background claim settlement and default General extension.
Existing physical cleanup, resource-guard, claim and cancellation tests remain
part of qualification. Definitions and formatting alone are not runtime
evidence; actual validation uses an explicitly granted Cargo batch, followed
by saving artifacts and cleaning its exact owned target.

The focused `--no-default-features --features subagent` batch passed 211
Subagent tests and 22 original `agent_tool` tests: 233 distinct tests, including
all 15 new definitions, with zero failures or ignored tests. Three controlled
restorations of the faulty execution paths each ran one selected test and
failed its behavior contract: a replaced-name factory, missing Team guard
propagation and the direct Teammate's missing keyed retainer. Compilation
errors and zero selected tests do not count as those counterexamples.

The actual `demo50_subagent_communication` run admitted the expected attempt,
delivered both uplinks and completed its terminal replay. Library/test Clippy,
production panic/unwrap/expect/unreachable checks, example Clippy, featureless
library compilation and final formatting checks passed without compiler
warnings. The owned target was cleaned after original owners/readers settled.
These selected results qualify this framework slice only. They do not inherit
the predecessor's full matrix or prove EKO/SDK integration, native services,
all features, release readiness or a future main commit's CI.

Rollback is a normal source revert without persisted migration. It restores
the separate-name-lookup race and removes host admission; it must not be
described as equivalent enforcement.

Source: https://echo-agent.dev/docs/adr-0098-project-file-system-adapter

# ADR 0098: Location-bound file I/O and execution resources

## Status and scope

Accepted implementation direction, 2026-10-25. Focused Rust qualification has
passed for the library/feature scope below; full Rust, consumer, native GUI,
real remote and platform qualification remain pending. The two modified offline
examples are not yet qualified. Earlier qualification of parent `939b672` does
not qualify these changes.
This decision implements the workspace project-workspaces Design/Plan; the
framework owns the reusable mechanism below, not EKO's location or SSH policy.

## Context

The standard file tools performed native filesystem operations after resolving
paths. A remote-looking path, a shell executor, or an open SSH terminal could
not change those reads, searches, writes, preimages or completion evidence into
remote operations. Each workspace host already has an independent ToolManager;
a new global current-project field or another tool catalogue is unnecessary.

Existing rules and Skills also read files before model/tool invocation. A Skill
can be discovered in one target and activated later: its descriptor's path text
alone cannot select its file or command source. The original physical command
cell owner must likewise retain its invocation's executor/resources after a
foreground observer stops waiting.

## Decision

1. `echo_core::tools::filesystem::FileSystem` supplies synchronous filesystem
   operations and portable metadata/entries in one immutable target namespace.
   Paths are namespace tokens, never an SSH address or proof of local existence.
   `echo_tools::filesystem::LocalFileSystem` retains native behavior and the
   original optional Git checkpoint implementation. The default stays local.
2. `StandardToolPack::with_file_system` and `ReactAgentBuilder::file_system`
   inject one Arc into the original file tools. The original schemas, budgets,
   parsers, effect reporting and per-call working directory remain authoritative.
   Git's private registration adapter delegates the original tool algorithms
   and schemas while consuming the same provider and original SandboxExecutor;
   public local Git tool constructors remain available. `list_worktrees` shares
   its original porcelain parser and reads markers through the selected Git
   executor/filesystem. Local captured-artifact roots are not remote grep scopes.
   Managed worktree mutation retains its original checkout/admin-directory
   guards, marker publication, caller-drop owner and exact compensation. The
   local `DirectoryIdentityGuard` wraps the original no-follow directory FD and
   stable identity verification. Current non-native enter/exit calls are
   unavailable **before reservation, merge or removal**, and say so in the tool
   description. They do not execute the native algorithm on a remote path.
3. Existing blocking operations retain invocation resource guards until physical
   completion. An async transport can bridge its existing runtime from that
   boundary. No additional runtime, retry executor, store, or task owner is added.
   `ReactError::Io` retains actual local error kinds; remote failures retain the
   existing `ToolError::RemoteFailure` / `ToolFailure` recovery facts.
4. The existing apply_patch parser, preimages, atomic replacement and definite
   failure rollback run against that provider. A possibly completed write is
   not a definite failure: report the typed uncertainty and attempted paths,
   without replay or speculative rollback. Checkpoints share one original
   format/index/permission algorithm through the filesystem and existing
   structured-command callback; an unavailable Git environment is not non-Git.
5. Existing InstructionResolver exposes a provider-aware fallible entry with the
   same precedence algorithm. Applications owning an InstructionProvider retain
   that owner and prepare through their existing blocking boundary. They disable
   the framework's automatic **local** rules loader after successful provider
   preparation; file-tool injection alone does not replace pre-model context.
6. The original SkillLoader/registry retain each Skill's file and execution
   source across discovery, activation, resource reads, inline commands and
   scripts. `discover_skills_with_sources` also accepts the caller's existing
   local executor for User scopes; it passes the Arc through the original loader
   into each source without creating an executor. Hosts can instead set the
   original Agent assembly's `set_default_skill_source` configuration once;
   ordinary descriptor/prepared registration captures that immutable source,
   even after the host execution backend changes. This value owns no invocation
   leases or I/O operations. Project and user/global
   sources stay distinct, even for identical path strings. The original parsers,
   policy, activation claims and registry
   remain authoritative; missing target execution never falls back to local.
   Existing HookRegistry entries also capture each Skill's executor and source
   directory. `bind_source_executor` permits hosts to bind existing UserConfig
   or Plugin entries explicitly. Mixed UserConfig definitions use ordered
   origin groups in the same existing source slot via
   `register_user_hooks_with_sources`; each event retains the original append
   order, and clear/reload replaces that source as a unit. Descriptor/prepared
   registration also exposes `with_source` entries for consumers that do not
   use discovery. Later host-wide executor replacement does not move a bound
   source; unbound public registrations keep their legacy default.
   Target commands do not inherit the client's PATH/TMPDIR or use native exists
   to decide whether their working directory is usable.
7. CommandCellRequest carries its actual executor and original resource guards.
   Runtime-only `SandboxCommand.resource_guards` and `cancel` are skipped by
   serde; backends transfer guards into their existing physical operation before
   spawning. The original cell supervisor requests cooperative stop and awaits
   the same backend/drain. After the existing five-second cleanup grace it
   reports an unsettled observation while retaining the active owner; finite
   wait calls keep the UI responsive. Dropping a future is not a cancellation
   receipt. Local cancellation reuses its original controlled child cleanup.

`run_code` validates persisted scripts against the same target filesystem. Its
existing minimum OsSandbox requirement and actual isolation receipt remain;
SSH alone does not establish OS isolation. Captured tool-output artifacts and
product persistence remain under their original local owners. Workspace-output
validation belongs to its real source, not a same-name local path or a model's
self-reported hash. No new Subagent registration or result-verification API is
introduced for parsing, which already clears model-claimed artifact authority.

## Alternatives and references

A parallel `remote_read`/`remote_patch` tool set duplicates schemas and policy.
Changing only path resolution leaves actual native I/O unchanged. Mirroring a
whole project invents synchronization and identity rules. Treating every host as
one global ToolManager invents unnecessary context fields. These alternatives
are rejected in favor of adapting the existing I/O and execution boundaries.

[VS Code Remote SSH](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/remote/ssh) associates
files and execution with a selected workspace target. [TRAMP remote processes](https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_node/tramp/Remote-processes.html)
associate process execution with the remote default directory. This framework
uses the shared location-adapter principle without adopting an IDE server.
The application's standard SSH/SFTP adapter owns authentication and connection
reuse; SFTP cancellation does not recall an already-sent write.

## Consequences and boundaries

FileSystem is a Rust extension surface. Its transport, credentials, workspace
revision and connection UI are application-owned. Metadata describes the target;
unsupported primitives fail explicitly. `open_read` returns a standard bounded
reader, without first loading the file into a Vec; evidence consumers retain
their original fixed-buffer hash and size algorithm. The default is Unsupported,
not a whole-file emulation. Provider readers retain their actual operation until
physical read/close settlement, including early observer departure.

The current standard SFTP interface exposes length, ownership, mode and timestamps,
but no stable directory identity comparable across a held handle and a no-follow
path reopen. Neither `realpath`, mode/mtime nor `statvfs` establishes the original
FD guarantee. Its default `retain_directory` is Unsupported. This is a concrete
framework public-menu limit, not remote-worktree acceptance; EKO's separate
existing TaskRuntime isolation path cannot qualify these tools by substitution.
Default local worktree tests and target list/mutation-refusal controls must pass
before qualification. No remote RPC, new cleanup owner or altered marker format
is added to manufacture capability.

The optional compare-and-swap primitive
reuses the original same-sidecar cooperating-writer lock; it does not fence
external editors or add an ABA/mtime contract. An error can occur after the
replacement, so callers cannot infer that bytes stayed unchanged. A remote
adapter without that exact primitive reports Unsupported. The currently developed client/remote
platform combination must be tested before claiming support for other systems.
Existing local, Docker and Kubernetes public options are retained.

New Rust API inventory and runtime-only fields do not automatically become SDK
accepted identities. SDK pins, accepted sets and language protocols are not
changed by this decision. Serde skip describes intended runtime-only transport;
actual collector/Host evidence remains separate from source inspection.

## Validation

Meaningful regression sources exercise the original tool pack with two distinct
namespaces sharing identical visible paths: read/list/search/diff/repo-map,
Unicode patching, actual checkout selection, stale preimages, definite rollback,
disconnection and an applied write with a lost response. Source-bound Skills
exercise discovery through activation/resource/script consumers, malformed
arguments before probes, unavailable executors and resource lifetime. Hook regressions invoke same-named source entries in
independent hosts, replace the host executor, and require captured executors/cwd
without local fallback when a required executor is absent. Mixed UserConfig
controls also require original append order, one source identity/count, and
complete removal on clear. Worktree
controls require actual target Git/list/marker I/O, disconnection without a
same-name native marker fallback, zero commands/reservations for unsupported
mutations, and detection of a native directory replaced at the same path. Bounded
reader controls consume non-ASCII target bytes through small buffers. The cell
regression observes a stop request while the original backend is held, then
releases that backend before expecting a terminal receipt and guard release.

The focused 2026-10-25 batch ran the Core (434), Execution (352), Orchestration
(532), Tools with files/git/shell (164), and root with
files/git/shell/project-rules/subagent (1,112) library tests successfully. Final
changes to Execution/Orchestration/Tools were retested together. Matching old
Skill production code failed the two intended behavior controls (7 passed,
2 failed); restoring the implementation passed the same nine controls. The
related five-crate all-targets Clippy check with warnings denied, independent
featureless/files/git/shell checks, and workspace formatting passed.

This is focused evidence, not the complete feature/platform matrix. The first
batch stopped Example 08 compilation at its fixed deadline and did not start
Example 09; those original outcomes remain preserved. A separately admitted
continuation then actually ran the existing examples with `--source-only` and
`--file-system-only`; both exited naturally with code 0 and no warnings on the
same Rust source. These offline controls cover source-bound discovery and the
provider-backed Unicode file read, without model or remote calls. The first
batch precisely cleaned its own target (5,165 files, 2.1 GiB; natural exit 0),
and the continuation did the same (2,217 files, 1.0 GiB; natural exit 0); neither
kept a warm target for review. Full matrix, dependency/semantic gates and
consumer acceptance remain required.
EKO additionally owns real GUI/SSH and same-name two-machine checks; fake
providers or a terminal login cannot establish that acceptance. The website
must mirror the finally qualified framework source, not invent a source pin for
this uncommitted candidate.

## 2026-10-30：read-before-edit沿实际owned工具提供路径事实

独立源码复核发现两个相邻缺口：成功target read effect被host canonicalize重新解释，
以及snapshot cwd与合法工具with_base_dir优先级不同。只给snapshot加provider getter
仍会在cwd=A、tool base=B时核错目标；不能删除base_dir能力或用host同名路径补证。

选择在原Tool trait提供一项同步default方法resolve_file_tracking_path，接该次最终
parameters／ToolContext，返回原FileSystem Arc及其namespace内路径。缺能力默认明确
Unsupported；既有文件工具只调用自身原resolve_path，ApplyPatch沿原root／action
resolver，不建立第二路径validator或来源表。调用在原blocking模式保留资源guard并
等待真实Join，map锁不跨await。该通用身份机制不依赖EKO的SSH／项目UI策略。

成功FileRead effect路径是已经报告的事实：ReadFileTool只把它绑定自身provider，不再
事后host／target canonicalize改写。原read-map扩为路径对应source／时间观察，未知
source只保诊断而不能授权。native按paths_are_native明确声明同一进程namespace，
non-native仅认同一保留Arc。30分钟TTL与每次prepare清空保持原规则，不新增registry。

公开record_file_read显式接source，这是Rust签名变化；FileReadHistory是原map值的
非序列化Rust类型别名，不是新wire DTO。ToolContext原16个accepted字段不增，三语言
既有FileRead／FileEdit String path和ToolResult effects保留。flag关闭不调用新hook，
成功effect即使来源证明缺失也不被抹掉或改成工具失败；guard开启时没有正确write
proof须依原Unavailable工具拒绝通道返回，不能猜host／snapshot或新增自动重试。
真实provider I/O错误保typed原首因，不泛吞成“未读”。

验证包括host／target双向alias、source相同路径隔离、base_dir A/B正反控制、相对／
绝对cwd、provider失败不落host、flag关闭和默认Unsupported的custom effects保真，
以及原TTL、资源与Join；真实SSH／SDK／native资格单列。本段是当前方案说明，不
以源码或结构校验替代同源实测与消费者复审，也不自动把新trait方法接受为语言路由。

## 目录范围合同补充（2026-10-30）

FileSystem 的不可变 namespace 决定读取哪一个目标；工具的显式目录根决定该目标内哪些路径属于本次读取范围，两者不能互相替代。Glob、RepoMap、CodeSearch 的 construction-time `with_base_dir` 继续作为上界；runtime `working_dir` 只作相对路径基准。Grep 保留原 base、working_dir 与 native artifact-root 的允许根集合，non-native provider 不纳入本机 artifact 根；没有任何根时保留无约束读取。

入口及递归实际读取目录项均使用被选 provider 的 canonicalize，复用现有路径 resolver 与 Grep 的原根集合，不新增 validator、权限模式或注册表。根内链接和同根 alias 继续有效；明确越界时整次调用返回范围错误，不返回已累积的部分成功结果。Glob、RepoMap 保留原逻辑路径用于 matcher、显示与分页身份。该检查沿用现有 pathname API，不声称能够原子防止检查后由外部并发替换 symlink；没有新增文件描述符身份或写入机制。

路径校验必须解析实际 I/O 的原路径，不在 provider canonicalize 前折叠 `symlink/..`；已展开的递归目录项不再次拼接相对 base。缺失写目标沿同 provider 解析已有祖先再重建后缀；普通无显式根仍保原 best-effort 行为。保留原忽略构建目录和悬空条目跳过规则，typed provider 故障继续传播。

验收覆盖原工具API的parent path、根/child链接、合法alias、相对base、symlink/..、Grep多根及目标namespace反例，并与旧生产代码使用同一断言；既有full/Glob matcher通过票不能替代目录范围验证。不新增公开API或产品配置，现成示例及官网工具用法保持，采用时由原作者核对对应说明。

Source: https://echo-agent.dev/docs/adr-0099-personal-weixin-channel

# ADR 0099: Personal Weixin protocol and durable no-stream admission

## Status

Accepted A+A2 design. The scoped Framework source review and focused checks
below passed; application recovery, native/platform and main acceptance remain
separate.
Root reserved 0099 after checking qualified 790 and local ADR occupation. The
qualified `0098-project-file-system-adapter.md` and the old Weixin 0098 frozen
source/review originals are preserved. Source definitions and direct rustfmt do
not establish consumer, native authentication, delivery or exact main acceptance.

## Context

The framework already owns `ChannelPlugin`, `ChannelManager`, `SessionHandler`,
original generation/fences, cancellation, the bounded sender and physical joins.
Personal Weixin needs native QR/authenticated-poll/send protocol. The fixed
first-party reference is [Tencent/openclaw-weixin 874637a0dbc24050f72d1385add4fc6170a2d726](https://github.com/Tencent/openclaw-weixin/tree/874637a0dbc24050f72d1385add4fc6170a2d726),
version 2.4.10 under its [MIT license](https://github.com/Tencent/openclaw-weixin/blob/874637a0dbc24050f72d1385add4fc6170a2d726/LICENSE).
Its host is not a Rust SDK or evidence that another client is authorized.
Authentication operations, scanner policy, durable task inputs, recovery and cron
notification selection remain application responsibilities.

An opaque response stream can wait for arbitrary time on HITL. Holding transport
capacity until response EOF blocks later `/reply` behind ordinary inputs. Letting
ACK release capacity while retaining one response task per input instead allows
unbounded producers. The original host, rather than the receiver, must retain
queued DATA and create long driver/renderers only after its original claim.

## Options

1. Install another Gateway/host or create a second inbox/executor: rejected;
   duplicates existing ownership and does not implement the native channel.
2. Hold each response until EOF, or release capacity on ACK but retain unlimited
   response tasks: rejected; respectively blocks controls or violates bounded
   producer retention. A different arbitrary response quota does not fix it.
3. Explicit fallible service binding plus no-stream durable admission: selected.
   Reuse the same factory/session/host, actual permits and original close owners.

## Decision

`MessageHandler::bind_durable_ingress(service_cancel)` is synchronous and
fallible. `admit_with_ingress(msg, cancel, receipt)` returns `Result<()>` without
returning a stream or waiting for model/HITL/output. Both default to Unsupported;
there is no legacy invocation as a capability probe. The unreleased old
`handle_stream_with_ingress` path is removed. Existing scalar/stream/reply APIs
and QQ/Feishu remain available with their previous opt-in behavior.

`SessionHandler::with_durable_ingress()` declares the factory capability. The
same wrapper binds one service child before transport acceptance. Each original
session generation and inner handler receive the same session child. Reset,
expiry, admission and close reuse one setup path and the original map/fences.
Inner bind failure stays with the original map entry and close obligation; it
cannot silently drop the factory owner, execute legacy effects or publish ACK.
Another service cannot rebind a live wrapper; a closed wrapper cannot revive.

The Weixin start path binds before accepting, spawning or polling. Parent Stop
first reaches the host through that child, closing new claims. Child cancellation
does not cancel its parent. Poll's original JoinSet contains only actual admit
calls, bounded by the existing 32 ordinary + 8 control permits. The permit stays
inside the real call until return, even after ACK; completed metadata is reaped
before each spawn. No transport response loop or per-input output waiter remains.
Media rejection feedback still uses the same original bounded sender.

Only the original input/control owner publishes `DurableInput`, `ControlHandled`,
`TerminalRejected` or `ControlRecoveryRequired`. The last fact means a durably
retained uncertain control effect, not success. Return, error, EOF, drop and
observer cancellation do not ACK. Strict batch cursor advancement still requires
every original receipt; a later ACK never passes an earlier Unknown.

A durable host persists queued DATA, publishes its original reply route and wakes
its existing claim owner. It retains actual long outputs/HITL and original sender
context/fences under its own execution limits; no admission spawns an output
waiter. Immediate control replies use that same sender. A framework-intercepted durable
reset keeps the original provider message ID in the existing
`OutboundMessage.reply_to` before handing the confirmation to its inner host; the
host can resolve and validate that exact message association, including explicit
None, without borrowing latest context. Legacy scalar/stream reset paths retain
their original behavior. `has_pending_work`
protects retained host work from idle pruning. Stop awaits admissions, original
send effects and the same handler close, including host drivers/renderers and
recovery initialization. Cancelling a stop waiter never detaches saved handles;
unknown settlement keeps its original owner and prevents Stopped/replacement.

`WeixinDeliveryHandle::validate_message_context(target, message_id, expected)`
validates the existing ProtocolState association without modifying it. Explicit
None needs a real persisted record containing `context: null`; missing record or
missing field is not absence. Some must match account/credential generation/peer,
message identity and exact reference, with the original readable content-addressed
token record. Missing/corrupt identity or token fails without HTTP, latest lookup,
state repair or secret return. Proactive sends and original captured-message
references retain their separate explicit APIs and the sole send producer.

The native protocol preserves authenticated-poll evidence, -14 reauthentication,
canonical account/peer identities, safe HTTPS/origin handling and secret redaction.
Send business acceptance remains Accepted/Rejected/Unknown. HTTP200, enqueue and
start are not success, and Unknown never authorizes automatic replay.

## Consequences

No new store, inbox, task FSM, queue, quota, executor or lifecycle manager is
introduced. The generic host must actually implement durability and physical
settlement; an in-memory ACK or EKO-specific empty stream is not that contract.
Queued DATA/index/route storage is not claimed constant memory. If the original
host cannot persist or accept input, the result remains Unknown and strict cursor
stops. Control liveness is conditional on available durable admission, not a
promise that finite/full storage can accept every arbitrary prefix.

A2 application recovery keeps one non-secret binding in the original Persisted
payload, including exact context presence, intent and saved workspace generation.
The original authority must positively prove never-claimed input and stable
account/context/environment before restoring its original claim/reply path.
Claim/effect/send uncertainty remains RecoveryRequired/Unknown with no replay.
These EKO policies and TaskRun resume fields are not added to Framework models.

## Testing and synchronized surfaces

Defined regressions use the real local HTTP poll/decode and sender entry, the
actual SessionHandler and a generic file-backed host fixture: 40 inputs and 128
single-message pages precede `/reply`, queued inputs are fsynced DATA, one original
claimed long response sends multiple chunks, and Stop waits its actual join after
a first waiter is cancelled. Another case holds admission after ACK to verify all
32 actual permits remain owned. Receipt drop/business Unknown, Unsupported start,
factory mismatch, child/parent cancellation, reset fences and context presence /
None / Some / missing or changed token remain distinct controls.

The focused Framework batch passed 135 channel tests (including all 10 new or
renamed NoStream cases), 12 root-facade tests and two compile-only doctests.
The existing demo38 typecheck, channel all-target warnings lint, strict
production panic lint, channel/featureless checks and workspace fmt/check passed.
Three precise lint repairs retained the initial warning and failed Clippy
originals. A later exact reset regression actually failed with missing
`reply_to` (None versus the original message ID), then passed after the
durable-only field forwarding fix. The full 135 channels, scoped all-target
warnings/strict production lints and fmt/check passed again, with another exact
clean. Earlier root-facade/doctest/demo/featureless results keep their original
epoch: no public API, legacy branch or example source changed. These results cover the retained Rust inputs, unchanged in this
documentation-only follow-up; they do not replace the full merge matrix.
Raw receipts and source identities are available only in this authoring worktree
under `.echo-semantic/local/weixin-no-stream-build/focused-actual/`; they are
not distributed runtime assets. The QQ/Feishu demo keeps its actual handler;
comments do not opt `AgentChannelHandler` into durability. Bilingual channel docs
track the API; website mirrors wait the coordinator's qualified producer. SDK
accepted contracts, real QR/login/messages, native GUI and exact main CI remain
separate and unverified by this source change.


---

Source: https://echo-agent.dev/docs/adr-0100-zstd-safe-chain-vendoring

# ADR 0100：由 Framework 维护 Polars 的 zstd 安全依赖补丁

## 状态

2026-10-27 用户明确采用本方案，继续正式设计与修复。本文记录已采用的架构方向；生产补丁、正式消费者 pin、完整依赖门禁与交付验收仍须分别取得证据，不能由 ADR 状态推定完成。

## 背景与参考

Framework 的 `data` / `statistics` 与 SDK 的完整 facade 消费 Polars。已发布的 `polars-arrow`、`polars-parquet` 0.55.2 约束 zstd 0.13；只更新锁不能选择 zstd 0.14.3。原链为 `zstd 0.13.3 → zstd-safe 7.2.4 → zstd-sys 2.0.16+zstd.1.5.7`。SDK 原锁的官方扫描在既有政策下仍报告四项漏洞和十项 unsound 告警，不能通过减少 data feature 或增加 ignore 解决。

本方案复用 [ADR 0089](0089-non-yanked-media-dependencies.md) 的发布包归属与唯一审计投影，保留其三个媒体依赖的相对 path 行为。Polars 属于另一种 Cargo 选择边界：[Cargo 官方覆盖规则](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/overriding-dependencies.html)规定 `[patch]` 仅由消费 workspace 根生效，依赖仓库中的 patch 不会自动继承；[Git 依赖规则](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/specifying-dependencies.html#specifying-dependencies-from-git-repositories)允许同一精确 revision 中的包被独立发现。因此 Framework 根使用两条 path patch，独立 SDK 根必须显式使用两条同 revision 的 Git patch。

隔离实验已证明两根完整依赖图可解析、真实 Arrow IPC 与 Parquet 压解三项通过，并在同一既有 RustSec 数据库上令十四项 zstd 告警消失。这不是正式来源、完整 Host、三语言、fresh 数据库或完整 yanked 资格；索引查询失败的原件与限制保留。

## 决策

### 唯一源码所有者与最小差异

Framework 在 `vendor/` 唯一维护两个官方发布包，版本及名称保持 0.55.2，仅把各自 normalized `Cargo.toml` 的 `dependencies.zstd.version` 从 0.13 改为 0.14.3，保留 optional、features 与其余声明。两包共 445 个发布成员，除这两个 manifest 外保持原字节，包括 Rust 源码、`Cargo.toml.orig`、VCS 归属和许可证；不复制反向父依赖闭包，不改名、不建立版本 shim。

| 发布包                | 原 `.crate` SHA-256                                                | 原上游 commit                              | 许可证             |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------ |
| polars-arrow 0.55.2   | `c5ab55460ca2553d1a2bbaf2046998cfbbb685bc18d1e168b4367b63301eb271` | `d7488c71ecfbc77790292ff5b365b991c08380ce` | MIT AND Apache-2.0 |
| polars-parquet 0.55.2 | `d33a17979d2afa0309437478662cf996361a6e1768bf467db82bd4f4a9443064` | 同上                                       | MIT AND Apache-2.0 |

原 archive checksum 证明发布来源，不证明修改后的整包仍与原 archive 相同。维护文档必须同时保存原包身份、逐成员校验及两处真实补丁。两包排除于第一方 workspace 成员；不为格式工具遍历而改写其它发布成员。

### 五个来源与同一审计权威

扩展现有 `vendor/registry-origins.toml`，保留 schema 1 和每项 `name`、`version`、`checksum`、`manifest`，准确包含原三个媒体父包及新增两个 Polars 父包。继续由 `scripts/generate-vendored-media-audit-lock.py` 拥有唯一算法，不在 SDK 或应用复制。

五项声明必须始终完整校验，但应投影集合取决于真实消费锁。原三个媒体父包继续必需；对于每个新增 Polars 父包，只要锁中存在该包记录，或任一实际 dependency 引用它，就必须纳入并核对恰一条精确版本及同源记录。只有该 Polars 包记录与全部依赖引用均不存在、确实未进入本消费图时才不投影；不得把被依赖引用的缺包静默跳过，也不加 CLI 专用 flag 或第二算法。该规则逐项判断，允许未来合法的 Arrow-only 消费图，不以三项或五项计数代替真实图检查。

当前 Framework/SDK 完整数据锁中 Arrow 和 Parquet 分别有 15 / 4 条父引用，正式修复后的这两个场景必须投影五项；当前 CLI 856 包锁完全没有两包及其引用，仍投影原媒体三项。完整五项声明与实际三项投影并不冲突，不能因扩大来源声明而阻断无 data 的 GUI 消费者。

生成器继续核对唯一身份、精确版本、原 checksum、vendor manifest 归属，以及应投影集合中每个 path/Git 父包与唯一 `echo_tools` 的同源关系；拒绝无关 fork、混合 revision、重复或应有却缺失的包、错误版本、非法 manifest 路径及覆盖输入。审计视图仅把应投影包的 source/checksum 转为原 crates.io 身份，保留真实锁由修订 manifest 解析出的全部依赖边和其它字段。旧三源生成器即使返回 0，也不证明数据图中的新增两包已被扫描。视图不用于构建、不提交为 Cargo.lock，也不替代正常 audit/deny。

### SDK 与公共边界

SDK 不复制 vendor，也不新增协议类型。取得 Framework 的精确、可恢复修订后，Host pin、SDK 根两条 patch、来源断言及独立锁/基线绑定必须共同指向同一修订，保持真实 canonical Git URL。正式合同生成与消费者验收不能仅靠改字符串断言通过。

`polars_parquet::parquet::compression::DecompressionContext::Zstd` 的 payload 仍是 `zstd_safe::DCtx`，但 safe7 → safe8 改变其 Rust crate 类型身份；显式持有旧 safe7 类型的第三方调用方不获原赋值兼容承诺。沿用原 `Unset`、`BasicDecompressor` 和已有私有 context 缓存，不增加 wrapper 或第二缓存。Framework 的 `load_dataframe -> DataFrame`、`is_numeric(&DataType)` 以及实际工具仍须编译和运行验证，不能称整个 Rust public API 等价。

SDK 当前保留的 5,352 项 accepted 身份、431 条路由及 18 个 data 操作由原合同控制。完整 Rust inventory 继续是遥测，不因这个补丁扩大跨语言接受范围；只有正式生成器确认的真实差异才能更新产物。接受集、source digest 与 pin 各有既有权威，不另建来源表。

### 修订恢复与交付资格

在当前禁止 push/merge 的授权下，可以先形成经门禁的 Framework 本地提交，保存 Git 对象、精确 tree 和可回读恢复材料，作为本地消费者候选。若验证采用任务级 Git 传输或自有 Cargo cache，必须保留实际对象来源、命令和 SHA，限本进程、不改全局；canonical URL/revision 与取得对象的传输来源分别记实。临时 `file://`、path 编译或探针提交 `7448e551...` 不能充当正式 SDK 来源。

本地对象可恢复不表示 GitHub 已发布、无本地补充的冷拉取可用或精确 main/CI 通过。若现有来源门禁无法接受受控本地候选，保留阻断，不删除断言或捏造远端回执；远端发布与冷恢复仍待相应授权。

## 候选方案与取舍

| 候选                                          | 取舍                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 等待上游发布兼容新 zstd 的 Polars             | 后续可移除本地补丁，但当前不能完成已知安全闭包修复                               |
| 只升级 zstd 锁记录                            | 父包版本约束不满足，无法形成真实解析图                                           |
| 删除 data/statistics、增加 ignore 或版本 shim | 缩小能力或隐藏原始身份，不符合已批准范围                                         |
| SDK 复制 vendor 或完整反向依赖闭包            | 增加源码权威和维护漂移；两个根显式选择同一 Framework 包已足够                    |
| Framework 两份最小补丁、SDK 根显式同源选择    | 已验证可行，源码所有者唯一、差异可审；接受新增 vendor 维护与 root patch 配置成本 |

## 影响、验收、失败与维护

正式实现须证明完整五项声明、按真实消费图投影及错误拒绝：Framework/SDK 完整数据图必须五项；真实 CLI 锁保持三项成功；完整图删除仍被引用的 Arrow/Parquet、重复/错版本/错来源均失败。随后分别验证真实锁图、完整标准依赖检查、原精确 duplicate 身份合同、实际 IPC/Parquet/context 恢复、Framework data/statistics 与示例、同 pin SDK 合同/Host/三语言消费者。probe 的 3/3 只能保留为可行性证据；五个 parent 的 checksum/yanked 补证不能替代整个锁图的检查。任何新风险、缺失组、来源或接受合同漂移均继续阻断，不能自动扩大风险接受。

失败时保留原日志、源码/锁/pin 的配对切点和必要制品，再在无读取者后清理准确自有 target；恢复只针对本任务文件，不覆盖其它工作或 SDK 既有候选。不能只回退 manifest 而留下新锁、来源断言或已宣告通过的验收。无 Cargo 产物的文档阶段不做形式清理。

本次没有新增用户功能或工具 schema；实现阶段仍须检查并同步所属依赖说明、原 data/media 示例与官网来源说明，不能宣称独立 root 自动继承 patch 或 registry 发布已可用。上游正式版本能形成安全闭包后，移除本地覆盖仍须重新验证来源、消费者及标准依赖门禁。
