Source: https://echo-agent.dev/en/docs/adr-0081-token-budgeted-compression-tail

# ADR 0081: Token-budgeted recent conversation tail

## Status

accepted

## Context and alternatives

A message-count split can put the active user request into the summarized
span when a single turn produces many tool results. Keeping all user messages
forever is unbounded; duplicating the EKO goal store in the framework would
create a second authority. Existing ContextManager, compressors, projection,
transcript and runtime-checkpoint boundaries already provide the owners.

The selected reference patterns are Codex's bounded retained user material
and reconstructed initial context, and Pi's token-budgeted recent tail with
tool-call/result boundaries and split-turn handling:

- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/53eaa297e595fc98df0f33d4c63686a7014d7c9a/codex-rs/core/src/compact.rs
- https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/compaction.md

These patterns support bounded raw material plus summary and reconstructed
authority. They do not require a second runtime or permanent raw user history.

## Decision

Extend SummaryCompressor, IncrementalSummaryCompressor and
SlidingWindowCompressor with `with_recent_token_budget`. Zero retains the
legacy constructor's message cap. One internal pure selector partitions old
and retained messages; it owns no state. Token mode retains older turns whole.
A large active turn may retain its exact request plus recent atomic execution
blocks. Its request may exceed the soft recent allowance, but cannot exceed
the hard input allowance. Such input fails explicitly, without text truncation.

`FrameworkConfig.agent.compress_window = 0` opts into a recent allowance of
25% of the live Agent window, capped at 20K tokens. Positive values retain
the legacy cap. Framework defaults remain compatible; applications choose
their default. Hybrid's configured stages share this allowance. Adaptive
levels retain their existing separate policy.

The automatic compact boundary reads the latest real request before horizon
folding and passes it as summary focus. Runtime notes and projections are not
user requests. Protected projections, canonical system context, transcript,
checkpoint and long-term memory keep their existing owners. A noncontiguous
selection does not pretend that its covered messages form one index range.

Manual focus and provider cancellation flow through one ContextManager
operation and one ReactAgent hook/trace lifecycle. Protected payloads are
subtracted before compression and the reconstructed result is checked against
the input allowance. Cancellation before transform commit preserves context;
product journal settlement after a successful transform stays application-owned.

## Impact and validation

Incremental calculation derives its previous checkpoint from accepted input
messages. Its `current_summary`/`current_structured_summary` cache is an
observation only. `ContextCompressor::context_committed` has a default no-op;
ContextManager invokes it after final budget/verification/promotion succeeds,
and on explicit restore/clear. Hybrid forwards the notification. A rejected or
cancelled candidate cannot publish this cache. Standalone compressor users
notify acceptance explicitly rather than treating calculation as a commit.

Runtime Hook notes and rich tool attachments use the existing runtime-context
marker, including multimodal text. Tool batches close over their call IDs across
these notes; no User-role image produced by a tool becomes the active request.
Cancellation is checked before calculation and before acceptance. A zero remaining
allowance fails before fallback can reinterpret zero as a legacy policy.

Existing Rust constructors and method signatures remain available. The optional
methods are reusable Rust API, with no new protocol, store or lifecycle owner.
EKO's goal/recovery state remains in echo-agent-cli. Rollback removes the new
opt-in config and restores the old constructors; transcript history is retained.

Regression coverage includes an exact Chinese request before a tool batch,
whole recent turns, a split active turn, oversized input, repeated summary and
incremental passes, protected budget accounting and pre-transform cancellation.

## 补充决策：必要投影与最终请求的可用性

有界引用能够避免将完整材料永久塞入 protected context，但读取引用必须在当前真实
请求中可用。原 best-effort 投影失败后继续的策略仍适合可选观察，不能代表所有输入
都是可选。框架因而在原 `PreModelContextProjector` 增加默认 false 的 `is_required`
与默认成功的 `validate_model_request`，复用原 compact/think 错误消费点和有限执行
生命周期。后者在最终请求构建后读取该请求与实际 artifact 配置，只核验、不改写。

候选比较：全局将旧投影错误变 fatal 会破坏原可选消费者；应用共享失败标志、文本
marker 解析或第二 validator 会脱离原 run 与调用；只确认注册表里存在 reader 会漏掉
本次工具上界或 final-only 的移除。所选默认方法保留未采用者行为，把必须性留给调用方。

选择 required 的失败沿既有 `AgentFailure.code` 传递
`required_context_unavailable`，不新增错误枚举、SDK 协议、store 或执行器。
原取消与物理未结算仍走自己的 typed 通道，不冒充来源缺失。应用用原暂停/恢复服务
消费该代码；框架不认识产品 TaskRun 或 NeedsInput。

本次已核实的一手模式依据是
[LangChain 官方 middleware](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/middleware/custom.md)
允许显式调用 handler、重试或重新抛出失败。将其用于必要输入失败阻断、可选输入
显式降级，是结合本项目既有错误和上下文边界的推论；该文档没有本项目同名 API，
也没有替本项目决定所有投影均为必要输入。

验证包括 optional 失败旧行为、required 错误停止、取消/未结算保留，以及在真实
最终请求中工具被移除时停止而模型零调用；本轮四项框架定向回归已实际通过。
EKO 的正式任务与普通聊天也已通过具名的缺失来源暂停、恢复及硬工具上界回归。
这些结果不代表完整有效要求、全部 consumer、SDK、全量 feature 矩阵或 main 已合格；
产品来源身份、作用域与版本仍由应用自身的实际 consumer 证据负责。

Source: https://echo-agent.dev/en/docs/adr-0082-lsp-response-value-fidelity

# ADR 0082: Preserve accepted LSP result values at the framework boundary

## Status

accepted

The SDK governance goal authorizes this contract repair. Focused implementation and red/green validation are recorded below; this
record is not full-gate or delivery evidence.

## Context

The live `StdioLspClient` request paths discard Hover.range, turn malformed
Location and Completion responses into empty lists, and decode JSON-RPC
`result: null` as though the result member were missing. Completion responses
also use official numeric kinds and `insertText`, whereas the simplified
framework type previously required an enum kind and snake-case deserialization.
This breaks framework consumers and the already accepted SDK LSP projections.

## References and comparison

Microsoft's LSP 3.17 specification is the authority, retrieved through the
GitHub contents API at official repository revision `f8c4bc9834703b7317c98c8e8053a28fa4b6b997`:

- [Hover](https://github.com/microsoft/language-server-protocol/blob/f8c4bc9834703b7317c98c8e8053a28fa4b6b997/_specifications/lsp/3.17/language/hover.md): result is Hover or null; contents supports MarkedString, arrays and MarkupContent; range is optional.
- [Definition](https://github.com/microsoft/language-server-protocol/blob/f8c4bc9834703b7317c98c8e8053a28fa4b6b997/_specifications/lsp/3.17/language/definition.md): Location or Location array or null; LocationLink requires advertised linkSupport.
- [References](https://github.com/microsoft/language-server-protocol/blob/f8c4bc9834703b7317c98c8e8053a28fa4b6b997/_specifications/lsp/3.17/language/references.md): Location array or null.
- [Completion](https://github.com/microsoft/language-server-protocol/blob/f8c4bc9834703b7317c98c8e8053a28fa4b6b997/_specifications/lsp/3.17/language/completion.md): array, CompletionList or null; kind is optional integer 1..25; insertText is camel-case.
- [Position](https://github.com/microsoft/language-server-protocol/blob/f8c4bc9834703b7317c98c8e8053a28fa4b6b997/_specifications/lsp/3.17/types/position.md): UTF-16 code units are the mandatory default when no other encoding is negotiated.

The official Hover and Completion forms and the existing framework structs are
sufficient. No new public parser API, dependency or SDK-specific parsing layer
is required. Cached lsp-types 0.97.0 independently uses the same optional kind,
Hover range and response variants, but is not a new dependency.

## Decision

Keep all protocol decoding in the existing framework request paths. The SDK
Host projects the resulting framework values and error; it does not infer
ranges, rewrite positions or repair malformed server results.

A present JSON-RPC null remains `Some(Value::Null)`; only an absent result
member means no result. Nullable method results produce None or an empty list.
Malformed required fields, coordinates outside LSP uinteger, reversed ranges,
arrays, JSON-RPC result/error signatures or completion values return the
existing typed LspError::ServerError with the method context, without returning
partial success or copying arbitrary server contents into an error.

Preserve Hover range and original zero-based coordinates. The client uses LSP's
UTF-16 default, so a Unicode position is not a Rust byte index. Hover strings,
markup values and ordered marked strings remain textual values; language-tagged
marked strings render into Markdown with safe code fences.

Change only CompletionItem.kind to Option<CompletionItemKind>. Absent/null kind
remains None; present numeric kinds map explicitly and unknown/invalid values
fail. Never manufacture Text. Decode insertText and documentation into the
existing accepted fields. CompletionList validates isIncomplete and items, then
uses the existing Vec-returning projection; the simplified API does not expose
completion-list metadata, resolve edits or incremental result streams.

LocationLink remains unsupported because this client does not advertise
linkSupport; a server sending an unsupported shape receives an explicit error.

## Alternatives

- SDK-side decoding would duplicate the framework's protocol projection and
  leave Rust consumers broken, so it is rejected.
- Keeping mandatory kind and inventing Text destroys optional-field evidence;
  rejecting a legal missing kind loses accepted behavior. Both are rejected.
- Replacing the whole public LSP model with full lsp-types would expand the
  contract and dependency surface beyond this value-fidelity repair.

## Impact and validation

The kind field signature changes within an existing accepted identity; it does
not accept additional Rust public identities. Whole-framework and CLI searches
found no other CompletionItem constructors or kind consumers at base 95ec66c6.
SDK contract generation must explicitly record this optional signature and the
three clients must preserve null; full inventory remains telemetry.

Eight focused Rust regression tests use the existing real Python stdio fixture:
range/Unicode, legal nullable results, malformed result errors, locations,
standard completion fields/optional kind, and JSON-RPC null-versus-missing.
The fixture's Python syntax and ten framed responses passed. The original six tests pass after five genuine pre-fix failures. Independent
review found error-member presence/drop and Serde tuple-shape counterexamples;
two new stdio regressions failed before the corresponding repair, then all
eight passed. The full LSP subset passed 28 tests with one existing opt-in
ignored, and focused Clippy passed without warnings. The existing demo55 executable example, root isolated LSP feature and
workspace formatting/check passed. Combined full merge gates, accepted SDK
consumer proof and independent review remain pending. Never interpret this record as exact-main or three-language evidence.

Formal English/Chinese LSP documentation changes belong in this repository.
The existing executable demo55 has no kind constructor or altered API call, so
its code needs no duplicate example; its existing test entry still must run.
The website mirrors those formal documents and must sync after the parent
publishes a clean verified framework successor, without bypassing its dirty
source guard.

## Independent review corrections

A present error:null is invalid, not an absent error. A malformed response with
an existing numeric request ID now settles exactly that pending request with
ServerError through the existing reader; it is not dropped until a transport
timeout and does not close other requests or the process. Unknown IDs are not
redirected to another request. Error objects require object shape before typed
serde decoding; tuple/array errors are not accepted.

Range, its two Positions and every Location require native JSON object shapes
before reuse of the existing types, because serde's generic struct visitor also
accepts arrays. Mixed valid/tuple Location arrays fail as one result. Additive
unknown object fields remain tolerated. A subsequent valid request is covered
in the malformed-result tests, proving request-local errors leave the existing
initialized client available.

## Diagnostic notification fidelity follow-up

Official Microsoft [Diagnostic](https://github.com/microsoft/language-server-protocol/blob/gh-pages/_specifications/lsp/3.17/types/diagnostic.md)
(blob 38bd1b3d3d1ce2fee270bf1759255146e41f9a6b) and
[publishDiagnostics](https://github.com/microsoft/language-server-protocol/blob/gh-pages/_specifications/lsp/3.17/language/publishDiagnostics.md)
(blob fbba90a322b804cd296daefbcb45d6aabf05dc61) were read in full.
The notification replaces a document's complete diagnostics; valid [] clears,
not merges. Severity is optional integer 1..4 and code is signed i32 or string.
The old generic serde path silently turns legal and malformed notifications
into [] because severity is a required Rust string enum and code is String.

The user's accepted-value governance authorizes Diagnostic.severity becoming
Option<DiagnosticSeverity> and code becoming Option<DiagnosticCode>, with a
closed tagged Integer(i32)/String value union. Numeric and text codes retain
their distinction, and missing/null remains None. This is an explicit supporting
field-value contract, not automatic acceptance of all new Rust helper identities.
The actual LSP tool consumer renders missing severity as UNSPECIFIED and uses
saturating line/column display arithmetic; no false Error fact is fabricated.

The existing per-URI diagnostics cache owns Result<Vec<Diagnostic>, String>.
A complete invalid update replaces old success with a typed retrieval error,
not [] or last-good. Next valid update replaces the error; [] explicitly clears;
other URI entries are independent. Native object/range/position checks reuse
this ADR's sole framework parser, and the whole diagnostic array validates
before insertion. No separate error cache, SDK decoder or authority is added.

A malformed envelope without a nonempty string URI cannot be attributed safely.
It ends the existing reader using the existing runtime/process settlement owner,
records last_error, rejects pending requests, closes the actual child, and makes
subsequent diagnostics retrieval fail explicitly. Addressable malformed values
remain URI-local and do not end the connection. Teardown clears the same cache.

Current accepted SDK Diagnostic identities contain range, severity, code,
message and source; no relatedInformation field is accepted or implemented.
The client therefore advertises relatedInformation=false. This corrects false
capability advertising without removing an accepted Diagnostic field. Full LSP
related-information/tags/data/resolve support is not silently claimed.

Four prepared real stdio regressions cover legal optional severity/code bounds,
atomic error/recovery/clear and URI isolation, fatal unattributable notifications,
and honest initialization advertisement. They use notification followed by a
request-response ordering barrier, not timing sleeps. The four regressions fail on the previous implementation and pass after this
notification repair; the whole LSP subset passes 32 tests with one existing
installed-server opt-in ignored. Focused/consumer checks and final independent
review, combined gates and actual SDK consumer proof are tracked separately.
Earlier request-fidelity checks do not prove this notification follow-up.

## Diagnostic terminal admission review correction

Independent review found a race after begin_terminal closes admission and clears
cache but before the existing cleanup owner has awaited actual child exit.
Runtime.running/initialized still correctly describe a live process in that
interval. Checking only initialized can fabricate [] from the cleared cache.
A read that started before terminal can also wait on the cache across this race.

Diagnostics therefore acquires the existing cache, rechecks the lifecycle fence,
then checks the existing runtime admission/initialized/cause under its lock.
That synchronous section is the read's linearization point: a terminal that has
already won returns its ServerError, while running/PID are never fabricated as
settled before actual exit. No second state or error authority is introduced.
Two real stdio tests hold the actual Child mutex to control teardown; one reads
after admission closes, the other holds cache to suspend an already-started
read across fatal notification. Both fail with old false clean success and pass
after repair. All six diagnostic tests and the complete LSP subset remain green.

Source: https://echo-agent.dev/en/docs/adr-0083-shared-tool-input-validation

# ADR 0083: Share canonical tool input validation with direct adapters

## Status

Accepted.

## Context

`ToolManager` already validates a tool's JSON Schema and then invokes its custom
input validator before execution. Direct consumers that call `Tool` themselves
cannot reach that private helper. The SDK facade omitted this step: an unknown
chart type was accepted and silently generated a line chart.

Validation is a reusable framework mechanism. Positional wire argument binding
and error conversion belong to the SDK adapter. Neither requires a new registry,
executor, permission policy, or schema maintained separately from the tool.

## Reference implementations

- [MCP Python SDK Tool.run](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk/blob/v1.x/src/mcp/server/fastmcp/tools/base.py)
  calls its existing argument-validation function before invoking the tool.
- [OpenAI Agents SDK function schema](https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/blob/main/src/agents/function_schema.py)
  associates the function with a typed parameter model and converts validated
  data into call arguments.

Both keep validation next to the authoritative tool definition. We reuse the
framework's existing implementation rather than copying it into adapters.

## Options

1. Copy JSON Schema validation into each adapter: creates multiple validation
   implementations and omits custom tool validators.
2. Construct a new ToolManager for every direct call: adds registry, timeout,
   retry and cache behavior to a boundary that only needs validation.
3. Expose the existing `validate_tool_input` helper: preserves the same schema,
   custom validator and errors without adding execution behavior.

## Decision

Make `echo_execution::tools::validate_tool_input` public. Existing ToolManager
calls stay unchanged; direct adapters call it before invoking their tool.
The existing framework re-export makes it available through the tools execution
module. No second validator, cancellation owner, or terminal authority is added.

## Consequences

Invalid input fails before tool side effects. Framework consumers remain free
to select their own execution lifetime. This Rust API does not automatically
become an accepted cross-language SDK operation; its inventory remains telemetry.
The SDK separately rejects excess positional arguments, including trailing nulls.

The helper's implementation is unchanged. Existing schema/custom-validation
regressions and direct-adapter counterexamples must pass before delivery.

## Chart dimension representation

The original GenerateChartTool stores dimensions as u32. Its schema now states
minimum0/maximum4294967295, and direct Tool execution uses checked conversion.
JSON Schema constrains mathematical integer values and their range; direct
execution additionally requires the serde_json integer representation, rejecting
floating representations such as1.0 explicitly rather than using a default.
Defaults apply only when an argument is absent. This removes wrapping/defaulting
of supplied invalid values while retaining zero and the complete original u32
range; it adds no resource limit, public operation or parallel adapter validator.

Source: https://echo-agent.dev/en/docs/adr-0084-acp-turn-steering-identity

# ADR 0084: Carry the reserved ACP Turn into the original Agent invocation

## Status

Accepted implementation decision; validation and delivery are tracked separately.

## Context

Standard ACP Prompts and SDK Run starts reserve one Turn through AcpSession.
AcpConnectionServices::prepare_run already records that identity in RunEntry,
ledger envelopes and the driver receipt. A text Turn without an invocation
context nevertheless selected the Agent's legacy stream method. ReactAgent
then allocated a different internal Turn UUID because runtime.turn_id was absent.
Tracked steering correctly rejected the mismatch between the original ACP Run
and that UUID, even while the real model request was active.

The SDK native counterexample parks the original loopback model request and
calls the public Run.steer method. Original Host bcb0389 reports accepted=false;
its own diagnostic log identifies the expected Session Turn and unrelated UUID.
A default Agent may legitimately not support steering, but that is not the
cause in this case: the default Host creates ReactAgent, which implements
tracked steering.

## Decision

Use the existing shared ACP preparation boundary to supply the already reserved
Turn as AgentInvocationContext.runtime.turn_id. RunStartSpec.run_id and the
TurnRequest identity must agree with the active Session lease before registry
publication. A caller-supplied conflicting runtime.turn_id is an explicit error;
it is not overwritten, ignored or mapped to a new identity. A matching value is
preserved. All other invocation fields remain in the original value, including
TaskRun run_id, lineage, working directory, cancellation, tools, history and
resource guards. Ordinary chat must not invent an application TaskRun identity.

Preserve legacy text Agent compatibility through the existing lower default
Agent::chat_stream_message_with_cancel method. Only Role::User with an exact
MessageContent::Text and all five optional metadata fields absent can use the
original legacy chat_stream_with_cancel path. Some(empty) metadata is present,
not absent. Parts, ResourceLink, Empty, non-User roles and metadata-bearing
messages retain the explicit unsupported error; no text flattening is allowed.
The outer invocation-aware default still delegates to the existing structured
method, so a concrete structured override always wins and retains its behavior.
No trait method, public DTO, wire operation or capability flag is added.

This is an observable dispatch change for ACP text callers: supplying the
canonical invocation selects the driver's already-existing Text + Chat + Some
branch, which invokes the structured method. An Agent implementing both legacy
text and structured overrides may therefore observe a different method and
output than before this identity fix. The trait's "same conversational
semantics" requirement means append/preserve context rather than reset; it
does not require those two overrides to return identical output. This decision
does not promise unchanged output for every third-party dual implementation,
and does not globally redirect invocation-aware text back to the legacy route.
The existing structured override and driver contract remain authoritative.

The fallback owns the original text in an async stream while the legacy stream
may borrow it across later polls. That fallback starts legacy setup on the
first stream poll; a legacy setup error becomes that stream's original error
item and the canonical Turn driver classifies it as Failed. It must not create
a successful terminal or replace the original error. Illegal structured inputs
remain an immediate method error. Existing cancellation and invocation guard
wrappers continue to own cancellation and lifetime.

## Alternatives

- Remove expected Turn matching: rejected, because it would steer the wrong
  original invocation instead of restoring identity propagation.
- Add an SDK-only identity map, a second Run or a task-local mutable context:
  rejected; the Session lease and value-scoped invocation already own these facts.
- Overwrite TaskRun run_id with the ACP Turn: rejected, because those are
  different identities with distinct canonical owners.
- Add a new text invocation trait method and forwarding paths: unnecessary
  API expansion when the existing exact lower fallback can retain legacy text
  behavior without bypassing structured overrides.
- Use as_text or error-string probing for fallback: rejected; that could erase
  multimodal/metadata semantics or misclassify a concrete implementation error.

## Consequences

This is a product-independent framework ACP mechanism, consumed by standard ACP
and the SDK Host. SDK clients remain thin transports; EKO policy and Task state
are unchanged. The existing turn-terminal and allocation authorities in ADR
0046 and ADR 0061 remain authoritative. There is no new persistent state,
scheduler, permission, source-acceptance obligation or error-code taxonomy.

The RecordingAgent ACP test fixture deliberately placed its cancellation,
barrier, tool and failure scripts only in the legacy method; its structured
override returned an immediate differently labelled answer for plain text.
The initial complete ACP integration run therefore passed 17 tests and failed
9 after invocation propagation. For these existing scripted tests only, the
fixture's exact metadata-free User/Text structured branch now delegates to its
own legacy script with the same cancellation token. All original assertions,
time bounds and Parts/ResourceLink rendering remain unchanged. Independent
review confirmed that test-fixture correction; it is not a new product rule
that dual overrides must behave identically. The core dual-override test still
proves structured dispatch once and legacy dispatch zero times, and the original
driver structured-chat contract remains unchanged.

Direct capture tests cover Chat/Execute and text/structured dispatch with the
reserved Turn, preservation of caller TaskRun/lineage/policy, and pre-publication
rejection of conflicting identities. Compatibility tests must prove legacy
text dispatch, structured override priority, strict message admission, owned
text/guard cancellation lifetime and original failed setup receipt. SDK native
three-language tests prove actual model-context consumption and concurrent waits
on one receipt; framework unit tests do not replace those consumer results.

No example changes are required because the APIs remain unchanged. Existing
ACP examples and the full framework gates remain delivery checks, and the
website does not acquire a new feature description. Diagnostic local path-patch
Host results are explicitly not published revision or SDK main proof; framework
publication and an exact SDK pin upgrade are still required.

Source: https://echo-agent.dev/en/docs/adr-0084-channel-owned-operations

# ADR 0084: Own Channel operations independently of registry borrows

## Status

Accepted.

## Context

The SDK held its ChannelManager mutex while awaiting a channel health callback.
That callback requested the same manager's IDs and could not acquire the mutex.
Start, send, stop and handler close had the same registry-lock boundary. Replacing
that mutex with an RwLock alone would not remove nested waits.

This is a generic framework ownership problem. The SDK must release its external
registry guard before invoking the original plugin; it must not copy the registry,
create another proxy, or own a second rollback/close state machine.

## References and options

[Tokio shared state](https://tokio.rs/tokio/tutorial/shared-state) separates short
state access from asynchronous operations. The [Tokio RwLock documentation](https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/sync/struct.RwLock.html)
also explains how nested acquisition can deadlock. We use one asynchronous lock
per original channel, with metadata independent of that lock.

Options considered were a second SDK lookup registry, fixing only health, a new
actor, and owned framework entries. The first divides identity and cleanup
responsibility; the second leaves other callbacks blocked; an actor adds another
execution model without a need. Owned entries reuse existing plugin behavior.

## Decision

ChannelManager keeps one map of ChannelHandle wrappers. Each wrapper references
one entry containing the original plugin, its handler cleanup responsibility and
the confirmed transport-stop epoch. The old get/get_mut accessors delegate to
this same entry, and remain available while owned handles exist. There is no
separate handler map or stopped-transports set.

get_owned, start_all_owned, stop_owned and stop_all_owned produce access or futures
that do not borrow the manager. Batch construction snapshots registered entries
synchronously. An unpolled operation does not invoke a factory or plugin. A later
registration belongs to the next batch. Results retain channel identity and one
failure does not suppress the remaining channels.

Lifecycle mutation uses the entry write lock. Health and send use its read lock.
Start stores the original handler before awaiting the plugin; failure or future
cancellation cannot erase responsibility. Stop records successful transport stop
before awaiting handler close, so close retry does not stop that transport again.
A mutable borrowed accessor advances a saturating epoch: an in-flight stop cannot
overwrite a newer invalidation, and saturation conservatively calls transport
stop. Successful shutdown does not unregister the channel. Manager or final-entry
drop can report remaining responsibility but cannot perform awaited shutdown.

## Metadata compatibility boundary

ID, label and capabilities are registration-time declarations and remain fixed
for that registration. Queries never await a plugin lock. QQ and Feishu use
constant/static capabilities; the SDK proxy uses immutable descriptor fields;
repository consumers have no live-changing metadata dependency.

The original trait could theoretically expose different labels/capabilities after
start/stop. Managed access now deliberately returns the registration declaration,
including through get/get_mut. Third-party plugins must use a new registration
lifecycle for a changed declaration. We do not promise synchronous references to
live data behind an asynchronous lock, use unsafe references or blocking locks,
or make get_mut disappear while an owned handle exists. Asynchronous calls still
reach the original plugin instance.

## Consequences and verification

Callbacks can query manager IDs and declarations after the caller releases its
registry guard. Independent channels do not share an operation lock. A callback
recursively awaiting mutation of its own channel remains unsupported; holding an
entry read lock while recursively awaiting a write can also deadlock. Callers must
not retain any external manager guard across an owned-operation await.

Regression tests cover all five callback boundaries, batch snapshots and lazy
side effects, independent entries, failed rollback, cancelled start/close, handler
retry, mutable-access epochs and the declared metadata behavior. Existing channel
examples retain the borrowed API and remain in workspace example compilation;
SDK adapter, three-language Host proofs and final exact-source gates are separate
consumer evidence. New Rust APIs do not expand the accepted cross-language wire
contract. Website publication follows the verified framework delivery snapshot.

Source: https://echo-agent.dev/en/docs/adr-0085-channel-handler-invocation-ownership

# ADR 0085: Original Channel Handler Invocation Ownership

- Date: 2026-10-13

## Status

approved

Implementation is authorized. This follow-up starts at the reviewed owned-Channel
snapshot `4eb005c`; it does not modify that prior milestone's frozen source or
reuse its checks as proof of the new API. Fresh validation and main acceptance
remain pending.

## Context

ChannelHandle owns the registered plugin and its handler cleanup responsibility,
but provides no forward entry into that handler. Merely cloning a handler Arc
would allow calls during failed start/rollback, after stop, or on a replacement
handler, and would make slow streams outlive awaited shutdown.

## Alternatives

1. Expose bare handler clones and ask callers to coordinate shutdown. This loses
   the original entry's admission and actual settlement responsibility.
2. Introduce another handler registry or executor. This duplicates an existing
   lifecycle authority and pollutes the framework with consumer address policy.
3. Extend the original entry with success-only generation admission and invocation
   receipts, using the existing cancellation and owned-stream patterns.

## Decision

Choose option 3. ChannelHandle exposes `handle_message`,
`handle_message_stream`, and `reply_message`. Each accepts the original message
and an invocation-specific CancellationToken. Single calls are driven by the
original generation's tracked task; streams return `ChannelMessageStream`, an
owned `BoxStream<'static, Result<OutboundMessage>>` plus its exact admission's
child cancellation token. The bundle implements Stream and offers into_parts;
adapters watch this same token while blocked on their own bounded sends, avoiding
old buffered delivery or shutdown deadlock without querying another generation.
This supporting Rust/Host representation does not expand accepted SDK identities.
Their driver captures the original
handler Arc and receipt and creates the trait's borrowed stream inside that
ownership scope. No transmute or leaked lock guard is permitted.

The original entry remains the only handler and cleanup authority. A small
generation admission/active-receipt record extends that entry, following
SessionGeneration/SessionStreamReceipt's synchronous RAII accounting. It has no
second handler map, business scheduler, durable state, or execution policy.
Start publishes cleanup responsibility before its first await, and opens
invocation admission only after successful start. Failed/cancelled start leaves
cleanup debt closed to new messages.

Each invocation has a generation child token. Cancelling one caller or dropping
its waiter cancels only that child. Stop retires generation admission and signals
all children before acquiring the entry write lock. After transport stop and
actual invocation receipt settlement, it closes the original handler. Failed or
cancelled close retains the same handler/generation for retry; restart creates a
new generation only after prior cleanup. Captured calls cannot switch generations.

MessageHandler's cancellation-aware single-call defaults preserve legacy method
semantics. Legacy calls may stop by dropping their local future; this proves no
external Run terminal. Implementations declaring `settles_on_cancel` must pass
the exact token to their underlying driver and continue until its real result or
stream termination. AgentChannelHandler's single-call override reuses its
existing AgentTurnDriver and terminal receipt, without a second Run runtime.
Uncooperative driven handlers retain shutdown debt instead of reporting success.

Metadata reads remain short and do not await handler locks. Recursively awaiting
mutation/close of the same entry from its callback is not supported. SDK wire,
resource address/generation, language catalogs, and EKO UI policy remain outside
the framework. New Rust methods do not automatically become cross-language
accepted identities.

Inactive/starting/failed-start admission and a mismatched message channel use
the existing ChannelError::InvalidConfig. A captured invocation whose original
entry generation was replaced returns typed ChannelError::StaleInvocation; it
does not borrow StaleDelivery's distinct session-output meaning. Adapters map
these to existing invalid-value/closed-handle categories without matching error
text. This Rust variant is Host-only inventory by default, not a new accepted SDK
wire error code. Missing Tokio runtime fails before admission/spawn, avoiding a
tokio::spawn panic.

## Industry evidence

[Tokio shared state](https://tokio.rs/tokio/tutorial/shared-state) distinguishes
short registry locks from operation ownership. [Tokio RwLock](https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/sync/struct.RwLock.html)
documents a held-read/queued-write/subsequent-read deadlock. Closing admission and
signalling cancellation before waiting on lifecycle locks avoids that dependency.
[Tokio shutdown](https://tokio.rs/tokio/topics/shutdown) and
[MCP cancellation](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/utilities/cancellation)
separate cancellation requests from actual settlement. The framework therefore
waits its original invocation receipts; cancellation notifications are not proof
of terminal execution or operating-system process cleanup.

## Consequences and verification

Regression coverage includes original handler identity, single/stream/reply
results, failed and interrupted starts, message channel mismatch, stale captured
calls after restart, child cancellation isolation, slow/full/unpolled streams,
setup failure, dropped waiters, actual driven settlement, close failure/retry and
metadata reentry. Bilingual framework documentation and the executable module
doctest demonstrate the public entry. SDK consumer delivery is separately tested
in its repository and pins a published framework successor.

Framework focused tests, workspace gates and the public-API feature matrix run
after the dependency repair/main synchronization. Current source preparation
does not claim they have passed. Website API descriptions and independent
Channel examples are checked at delivery; existing borrowed APIs stay supported.

Source: https://echo-agent.dev/en/docs/adr-0087-telemetry-subscriber-composition

# ADR 0087: Compose process telemetry with an existing subscriber

## Status

accepted for the SDK governance repair on 2026-10-14 after independent design review (0 findings).

## Context

A Host has a stderr tracing subscriber before an accepted telemetry initialization request. Replacing the global subscriber fails; dropping the already-built metrics provider synchronously during rollback blocks the ACP dispatcher. The existing framework owns METRICS, providers, sampling and one-shot lifecycle.

## Decision

Expose a Rust/Host-only stable composition layer and read-only console filter. Formatting has one writer with the existing diagnostic filter OR the console filter; it is not duplicated. Standalone exporters/providers must be ready before installing a subscriber, and failed installation completes rollback without publishing globals. Delegate Tracer and PreSampledTracer operations to the existing runtime using standard BoxedTracer/BoxedSpan, and use standard per-layer dynamic filters. The OTel layer is never wrapped in reload, preserving context downcast. Host-provided console writers choose stderr; standalone initialization preserves its original console behavior. Initialization and shutdown retain their existing API and one-shot semantics. No public language contract or additional telemetry state authority is introduced.

## Alternatives and tradeoffs

Ignoring subscriber failure, exporting only metrics, removing diagnostics or writing console output into ACP stdout breaks existing behavior. Reloading the entire OTel layer loses required downcast support. A stable composed layer uses the existing tracing/OpenTelemetry implementations without copying ID generation, sampling or export scheduling. The approved design is copied to docs/telemetry-composition-design.md for independent repository review.

## Consequences

Existing init/shutdown signatures and one-shot lifecycle remain unchanged. The new composition helper is Rust/Host-only. The SDK must explicitly pin the published framework change and prove real collector receipt and blocking-job ownership.

## Validation

Verify real collector receipt, shutdown flush, valid parent/sampling context, initialization boundaries, standalone/external-subscriber errors and rollback. SDK blocking jobs use the original Host settlement owner; cancellation does not prove completion. All source and delivery gates remain required.

# ADR 0088: Cancellation observation does not own physical settlement

- Date: 2026-10-15
## Status

Accepted; user explicitly selected option B and authorized implementation/delivery.
- Design: [Subagent physical settlement](../supreme/specs/2026-10-14-subagent-physical-settlement/design.md).

## Context

A local dispatch JoinHandle can finish after abort while a detached producer is still cleaning. Releasing claim/interruption/permit on that local fact permits overlapping effects. Historical held-cleanup evidence exposed this conflict with the physical-stop-before-CAS guarantee of ADR0060. Existing Task lifecycle states and execution owners already express pending cleanup.

## Decision

Keep the original RuntimeTaskService/RuntimeDagExecutor/SubagentExecutor owner through original stream closure and exact CAS. The configured cancellation grace bounds only an execute/settlement observer, starting once at its first admitted root or exact cancellation scope. Exact A does not start sibling B's run deadline. Normal execution has no observation clock.

Expose the Rust observation `ReactError::ExecutionNotSettled { run_id, execution_id }`, never an Agent terminal. Observer expiry cannot fabricate Cancelled/Paused/Failed, release a claim or trigger mutation retry. The existing owner keeps permits and cleanup; repeated requests do not extend the deadline. Parent drop/unwind signals then drains, never aborts solely because observation grace elapsed. Loss of authoritative closure remains AuthorityUnknown, including restart and disconnect; it cannot launch a replacement attempt.

This refines ADR0058/0060 forced-abort wording: only physical completion permits settlement. Existing execution timeouts still determine cause but do not destroy the sole cleanup future. No new TaskStatus, scheduler, store, backend authority, SDK API or accepted wire identity is introduced.

## Alternatives

Forced abort with a new durable physical-receipt protocol would require another interface and was not selected. Retention can hold existing capacity forever for non-cooperative code, which accurately exposes the existing work rather than releasing its effects as if stopped. Operators may need authoritative backend/process shutdown. Tokio shutdown/JoinHandle and Python cancellation patterns referenced by the design separate cancellation notification from completion.

## Consequences

Examples and website do not acquire a new product feature. Existing callers must handle a Rust observation error without terminal conversion; SDK error-detail adaptation is tracked independently. Required tests cover held cleanup, root/exact isolation, caller lifecycle, cause order and unknown recovery on the current source.

## Rust migration

Replace infallible `AgentFailure::From<&ReactError>` with `TryFrom<&ReactError>` and make `AgentEvent::from_error` fallible. A nonterminal observation has no valid AgentFailure value: refusal preserves its run/execution identity and converts back to the same typed ReactError. All existing actual terminal errors keep their exact fields. Migrate direct and into-style consumers; never substitute Failed, Other, panic or a new terminal kind. Event normalization passes an original observation Err through without synthesizing missing-terminal failure. Team timeout and dispatch/result boundaries propagate it without releasing the original physical owner. Existing Rust consumers must explicitly handle the fallible API; SDK Host adaptation and accepted cross-language membership remain separately owned, and CLI compilation is part of consumer validation.

`AgentTurnDriver::drive` changes to `Result<TurnReceipt>` at its actual setup/stream/sink observation boundary; ordinary receipts remain unchanged and consumers propagate the refusal. Internal Team dispatch must not mistake a nested runtime observer timeout for physical closure: `RuntimeTaskService::execute_to_settlement` shares the one original private spawn helper with `execute`, but waits the original join without an observer timer. Public external observation remains bounded. The owner-composition method is not a language API or a second scheduler/store/registry, and callers must not execute again to recover a timed-out owner's result.

Foreign Agent setup can expose not-settled identity without returning a stream. There is no canonical future to invent or re-execute. ACP retains the original active Session lease within the existing RunEntry's uncertain-owner resource slot and keeps Running/no receipt; only authoritative receipt/fence releases it. Admission, close and restart must not infer completion from missing process-local control, disconnect or revocation. No permanent pending task or mem::forget is used to simulate ownership; other framework consumers preserve their own existing resource/fence authority.

### ACP Run errors and connection lifetime

The official pinned `agent-client-protocol` 2.1.0 `ConnectionTo::spawn`
contract shuts down the entire server when a spawned task returns `Err`.
Its JSON-RPC request responder instead returns an error for one request. A
driver's nonterminal Run observation belongs to the latter scope; it must not
make unrelated Sessions or bounded Run observers lose their connection.

Keep the original `RunEntry` lifecycle mutex and its existing Running/Settled
states. Running can retain the driver's structured ACP error alongside the
original Session lease. `RunEntry::wait_result()` exposes that observer result
to Rust consumers, with a committed receipt taking precedence; it does not
declare physical completion or permit retry. The lease and observation are
recorded under the same lifecycle lock, and registered waiters are notified.
Receipt-only `wait_receipt()` and shutdown continue waiting for real settlement.
The standard Prompt consumes `wait_result()` before and after request
cancellation, returning its error through the existing request responder without
persisting a fictional receipt. The shared prepared task returns `Ok` after
recording a Run error, so SDK Host's existing `spawn(task)` stays usable.

Returning the original Run error from the actor task kills the connection;
logging it and returning `Ok` alone loses diagnostics and leaves Prompt waiting
forever. Creating a Failed/Cancelled receipt would release uncertain physical
ownership. Those alternatives are rejected. Ordinary Agent errors still produce
their original Failed receipt; real spawn, transport and responder errors keep
their existing propagation. This is an ACP observer API refinement within B,
not a new Run state, store, wire method or accepted language contract.

Root interruption adds required `RuntimeDagController::request_task_interruption(run_id, task, claim, disposition) -> Result<bool>` to delegate to the existing exact-claim request CAS without terminal settlement. True is same-claim durable admission, false is supersession, and errors retain the original claim/unknown. No default success or alternate state mutation is provided. Store/Team/SDK/CLI controller source implementations migrate explicitly; no new wire operation is introduced.

Original attempt projections retain shared/local permits and physical-closure knowledge through uncertain exits; neither a string error nor durable claim disappearance releases physical ownership. First request clocks require successful admission. React retains steering and execution resources in the existing close authority, fences new turns and reports unknown on close; no new scheduler or parked replacement task is involved. All opened stream sources drain through actual EOF before ordinary terminal/cancellation receipts as well as observer errors.

Shared admission uncertainty survives observer/service destruction in the original KeyedExecutionAdmission key/generation state. Opaque owner/generation fences are queryable, and only authoritative original physical completion/backend fencing permits a matching clear; stale/wrong-owner proof fails. InputReceipt waits become fallible Result without adding public input states: the original watch carries private refusal identity, wakes existing observers, and never fabricates Dropped/Drained on sender loss. Ordinary real input and terminal states retain their fields.


### Existing Tool/Sandbox projections

The accepted nonterminal error must also bypass existing Tool/Sandbox error-to-result adapters and React callback/transcript publication. Private result plumbing may be fallible or absent for an observation, while ordinary tool results and the public ToolFailure shape remain unchanged. Unknown physical work is not a completed tool failure or permission to continue the LLM. This is the same B settlement boundary, not a new tool policy or API.

The canonical started/draining Tool path keeps its existing execution future and permit through configured timeout, React cancellation grace and batch timeout. These boundaries signal cancellation and retain the first business cause; they do not drop physical work. A streaming Complete is retained until the same stream reaches actual EOF. Only this canonical draining path changes; public ordinary non-draining bounded behavior remains unchanged.

The same started/draining owner survives output receiver closure: retain the original future and permit, signal only its child cancellation scope, stop delivery and return the first delivery cause after physical EOF. ToolManager adds an embedded resource projection through the existing KeyedExecutionAdmission mechanism for unknown/unwind retention; its existing read/write semaphores remain the sole quota. No additional threshold or execution registry is introduced.

ACP Session close preserves observation identity in its original close receipt and generation. Repeated begin/finish/close_all observation cannot resend a close mutation. close_all drains all originally admitted closes, preserves each unknown receipt and returns an original typed observation before aggregating ordinary failures. Lost close-owner authority without a run identity keeps the same receipt/Agent/resources and waits on its existing Notify; no synthetic identity or replacement owner task is introduced. Ordinary returned close failures may retry as before, and genuine successful close releases the Session as before.

Headless convenience observations carry the original `HeadlessRunHandle` privately on the returned `HeadlessResult`, accessible through `retained_owner()`. Its existing five public value fields and formatting/exit behavior remain unchanged; external Rust literals use `HeadlessResult::new` after the private owner field is added. The state stores an owner-free observation and only outward wait results attach that same handle, so there is no state/result ownership cycle. A successful real close releases the Agent; an observation keeps the same Agent/ToolManager/resource authority instead of silently destroying it when `run_headless` returns. Waiter cancellation leaves the original task in control. A caller that may stop waiting and still needs subsequent uncertain-owner observation must use `start_headless` and retain its handle; a cancelled convenience call has not yet transferred an outgoing owner and cannot promise one after every parent owner is destroyed. Callers explicitly retain the returned observation's original parent owner; dropping all such owners does not establish physical stop and no automatic recovery or new late-proof interface is promised. This Rust-only owner projection is not automatic SDK method acceptance.

### Original live-source completion after observation

An intermediate source observation is not a permanent failure cause. Continue the same immutable source and existing normalizer; only a later explicit original terminal after its latest matching run/execution observation, together with actual EOF, can discharge that source knowledge and let its original owner settle the original input/receipt/exact claim. Source and sink observations are different authorities. A projected missing-terminal/error, cancellation notification, delivery completion/failure, foreign owner/generation, or EOF alone cannot clear unknown. A later source observation invalidates earlier closing knowledge. Preserve the first real business cause and original terminal value fields; no replay/re-execution or new generation/proof API is added.

The existing Core wrappers retain necessary original terminal confirmations and observations through physical drain. First cancellation keeps its cause but defers its one cancellation terminal until the source really closes; with unresolved observation, a genuine original terminal after the latest observation is additionally required. Without such proof EOF cannot synthesize cancellation. Earlier real terminal/error is preserved and the existing normalizer still delivers at most one canonical business terminal. The original RuntimeTaskService supplies bounded observation; no new wrapper timeout or owner is introduced. Setup errors with no source and unresolved delivery authority keep the existing Unknown behavior.

## Scheduler occurrence consumer

New scheduled/manual occurrence payloads explicitly opt into the physical-settlement contract in the original journal before callback effect admission. The private versioned wrapper makes old decoders fail closed; real old flat payloads remain legacy at-least-once and are not silently upgraded. Original protected EffectStarted cannot be reconciled into an automatic retry merely because an observer, callback task, process-local hint or connection is missing. The existing DeliveryRecord and SDK operations remain unchanged. The necessary canonical EffectStarted optional payload field described below is a Rust source migration.

One original callback owner follows the existing owned-mutation spawn/join pattern and keeps the original claim, callback guard, FireFn dependencies and store/control owner until the real callback result and original settlement. Borrowed waiter drop and cancellation do not drop/requeue that callback. Typed observation bypasses last_run and terminal settlement, retaining the protected occurrence/attempt fence across reopen. True known result/error preserves existing projection; owner loss yields nonterminal observation using the original SchedulerInvocation occurrence/attempt identity. Source-less returned observation has no invented late-proof API. Scheduler join/shutdown does not turn loop exit into physical completion while protected claims remain.

The cost is explicit: new protected effects with no physical receipt do not regain automatic at-least-once replay after owner loss. Actual old flat journal records retain their old policy; new admission/abort fixtures must not be relabeled legacy. Generic callback signature, Task status, quotas and workflow protocol stay unchanged. This is the direct Scheduler closure of the already selected B contract; Workflow protected-claim option A was separately accepted by the user, bound to original SDK proposal SHA256 23c5a59ae405ecd71c3e79b6d945e77e8b7927e0e1f0176ad91047147341a09f; it is not implemented or validated by this Scheduler slice.

Scheduler handle-only callers must retain their existing parent when shutdown reports observation. The handle therefore holds the original Runner Arc; join/shutdown borrow `&mut self` rather than consuming it. Pending waits borrow the original Option<JoinHandle> without taking it; only actual completion consumes/caches the loop join. Repeated observation neither repolls a completed join nor re-executes callbacks. FireFn/store/control/occurrence roots remain reachable from the same handle; explicit destruction of that last parent is a caller boundary, not an immortalization promise. CallbackOwnerGuard remains a weak liveness hint; protected journal state remains authoritative after the callback has returned unknown. This necessary Rust receiver migration updates actual immutable call sites, without adding SDK scheduler wire/API membership.

A legacy occurrence newly executed by current code is not exempt from B. The true current-callback counter returned typed unknown but remained legacy and was reclaimed with a different attempt while the same file backend was held. Canonical DeliveryEvent::EffectStarted therefore carries an optional replacement_payload, applied only after original exact-claim/Claimed validation in the same journal event; Scheduler uses it to protect the new current attempt. Recovery retains its original Claimed+EffectStarted atomic batch and protects that newly admitted attempt there. Ordinary begin_effect/prepare_transition uses None (serde default/omit) and old event bytes stay unchanged; old deny-unknown decoder rejects Some, and protected checkpoint payloads reject old flat decoders. Existing Rust literal/match consumers migrate the optional field; no SDK event acceptance or new recovery API follows automatically. Historical old effects may have their original first replay, but a new callback effect never runs without durable protection. Wrong claim cannot alter payload/sequence, and projection-only migration is prohibited.

## Workflow protected-claim follow-up (accepted A)

The user accepted A, bound to the independent SDK proposal original SHA25623c5a59ae405ecd71c3e79b6d945e77e8b7927e0e1f0176ad91047147341a09f/7288B. Its later maintained acceptance header is not the old whole-document digest. Two real native Memory/File Graph counters show the original file backend still held while the same checkpoint can be newly claimed; both exit101 after releasing/joining the original backend. They prove the generic Graph/Store defect, not SDK DSL Function support or registered-Llm Host execution.

Reuse the same Store claim authority: default-false supports_protected_claims and explicit unsupported protect_claim(id,attempt), native private protected phase, Graph-bound bool projection, capability before executable claim/prefork, positive exact-attempt protect before Node. Deferred/Rejected and fresh entry qualifications remain distinct. Protected attempts do not expire/replay; normal physically closed errors still requeue. Delete/save/clear cannot destroy active protection; mixed clear atomically refuses and stale settlement cannot clear a later attempt. File uses its original directory fs2 lock and atomic writer through actual I/O completion despite observer Drop; visible-but-not-durable writes are not success and repeated protection must complete the barrier. Versioned private bytes reject the old automatic reader; old delete/clear are explicitly unsafe, so downgrade cannot use an old writer on protected data. Memory remains instance-local; no new recovery query or forced unlock.

Heartbeat error and the existing Node timeout/cancel/fanout/receiver-close paths must signal and drive the same future/source to physical EOF, preserving first cause and typed uncertainty; no dropped source is an ack/requeue receipt. Agent Node uses existing invocation identity and raw source provenance, never a synthetic terminal as closure proof. The same Node lifecycle repair applies to fresh accepted entry points without adding a Store capability gate there.

This is a necessary Rust API/remote persistence contract increment, not an automatic language-inventory acceptance. The SDK's one new protect reverse operation and protected_claim_v1 capability will be implemented and verified in the independent SDK lane. The accepted cost is indefinite blocking after protected owner loss, even between protect and Node start; ordinary legacy unprotected recovery and known-close retries stay. Shared File locks, durable directory setup and platform-specific fsync limits are explicit; no blanket exactly-once or cross-platform power-loss promise follows.

Graph retains its existing immutable Node/Edge capabilities through private Arc definition leases. One owned original-loop invocation backs each public operation; a borrowed waiter or polled stream Drop signals the same operation but does not drop its Node future. The stream starts its owner on first poll. Public signatures remain unchanged; no public Clone/handle, execution registry or second engine is added. An operation join loss is typed knowledge, and source-less unknown still requires the caller to retain the original Graph parent. Last-parent destruction and runtime/process shutdown do not become physical closure proofs.

# ADR 0089: Keep media builds on a non-yanked ZIP dependency

## Status

Accepted on 2026-10-16 for the dependency-policy failure at framework main
`875cc22f2e99c7ccd83c07e02c03fe221c5e3f6c` (CI run 38849170013).

## Context and alternatives

The existing XLSX writer, XLSX/XLSB reader and DOCX implementation depend on
zip 2.4.2 or 8.6.0. The official crates.io index marks both releases and all
compatible releases as yanked; zip 9.0.3 is the available non-yanked release.
The current published and upstream-main media parents still select older ZIP
majors. A lock-only update cannot satisfy their constraints. A root-only Cargo
patch would not propagate to independent Git consumers of this framework.
Ignoring yanks, changing audit policy or adding a version shim would conceal the
failure rather than repair the dependency closure.

## Decision

Keep the exact published parent versions as checksum-attributed source under
`vendor/`, use relative workspace path dependencies inherited by `echo_tools`,
and select zip 9.0.3. Exclude these third-party packages from the framework
workspace and make their manifests standalone for Cargo's formatter traversal.
Preserve their production source/includes and licenses; remove dependency-unused
upstream development targets. The complete provenance and local adaptation list
is in [vendor/README.md](../../vendor/README.md).

Calamine's private path-cache helper propagates zip 9's fallible filename iterator
through its existing ZIP error conversions. Six private rust_xlsxwriter return
lifetimes are made explicit to remove warnings previously hidden for registry
dependencies. Its optional zlib backend uses zip 9's corresponding feature name.
First-party media tool APIs, results and feature meanings remain unchanged.

## Consequences and maintenance

This source override belongs to the framework build boundary, so Git consumers
resolve the same media implementation without a second root patch. No runtime
state authority, accepted SDK operation, source allowlist or audit exception is
added. Official scanners skip path/Git packages; an additional temporary
registry-origin view restores the three published parents’ conservative
name/version advisory coverage with the same official scanner. It binds each
parent’s original SourceId to the actual `echo_tools` owner, refuses mismatches,
and projects only source/checksum. The actual lock and normal audit/deny gates
remain intact. Python 3.11+ is development audit tooling, not a framework or
Python SDK runtime dependency. A targeted Cargo update also rebinds five existing-version dependency
edges permitted by upstream ranges; they are recorded in the provenance note
and are not all required by ZIP itself.

Maintain the archive provenance and small local delta when updating these
sources. Remove the override once official releases provide a non-yanked closure
and pass the media, dependency and workspace checks. Cargo registry packaging
removes local paths and would fall back to the original parent releases, so this
change does not make registry publication ready or change release scope.

## Verification and documentation scope

Persistent integration tests exercise actual XLSX write/read and DOCX pack/read
with Unicode and numeric content. Independent consumer resolution and full local
workspace/feature gates plus exact merged-main CI remain separate requirements.
Public examples, SDK contracts and website instructions do not change because
media entry points and behavior do not change; existing examples remain in the
workspace all-target gate. No raw diagnostic archives belong in Git.

# ADR 0090: Retire only A2A and LSP after consumers remove their dependencies

## Status（2026-10-24 历史原记录）

Accepted product direction on 2026-10-24; implementation has not started in
this documentation contribution. At framework baseline
`51726454985fd6f064b21a7e9c539e22d494c987`, A2A and LSP still exist and remain
available. This record neither removes an API nor proves consumer migration,
merged-main CI, or release acceptance.

## 2026-10-28 后继源码实施同步

本节与已批准的完整F30物理删除包共同采用，采用前须由Framework唯一writer核对真实source。
A2A／LSP的feature、模块、公开facade、专属example及LSP插件专属字段退出，不使用空成功shim。
旧`lsp.yaml`仍由原cold prepare的`PreparedPluginDocument`冻结、hash并在同generation私有
容器持有，通用diagnostics保完整错误/路径/身份；缓存和invalidation仍原owner。健康同级
组件与publication/rollback/shutdown保留，ProjectRoot/Instruction/scope及其它合理API不删。
SDK接入此删后源时应只原样投影diagnostics，不再依赖`lsp_config_file`或追加自造退役事实。

EKO独立TUI/REPL/CLI/JSONL退役属应用包；GUI内置终端、Agent shell、桌面最小参数、IM、
cron、共享恢复和独立SDK Host stdio继续保留。没有新增executor、Store、CRUD或权限闸。

以下原5172645基线表与早期桥接段落均属历史对照，不再表示当前可调用API。固定tag/分支、
Exa独立提交与用户数据不改。源码采用／文档同步与删后构建、正常锁、依赖策略、SDK正式
删除源Git pin、native、main CI和发布是独立资格；本节不据旧focused或受控Host宣告完成。

## Context and authority

The approved EKO product direction keeps the desktop GUI as its user entry
point, with IM receive/send and scheduled tasks. EKO's independent TUI,
REPL/interactive CLI and JSONL product surfaces are to retire. Its embedded
terminal, Agent shell execution, MCP, shared Task/Subagent execution and
recovery remain. Desktop startup arguments and the independent SDK Host's
stdio protocol are not those retired EKO product surfaces.

The same explicit decision retires A2A and LSP from the framework, SDK and EKO.
It is a narrowly approved exception to the framework's public-API preservation
rule, not an inference that anything unused by EKO is dead. The framework
continues to serve independent consumers. In particular, ACP is a different
protocol and remains supported; A2A retirement does not retire ACP.

This record implements the already approved product-boundary-contract outcome
of the cross-repository EKO GUI convergence design. The immutable execution
inputs were checked with these SHA-256 values:

| Input | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `design.md` | `1add234fe9bd5bbf6865cbddcad63f59b7c7264eba2e8fa245d13fd4daf12031` |
| `plans/plan_01_product-boundary-contract.md` | `22773834501db005dd567c99d23b338c659e752a5bd08e3ee9eb417a4c7f24a1` |
| `plans/delivery-map.md` | `cd50060800b1d9faa28076815139a6f690489ecb8f4424f6672d54b3ffbacd61` |

Those files belong to the workspace's phase materials under
`docs/supreme/specs/eko-gui-product-convergence/`; this framework ADR owns the
long-term framework retirement boundary. It records an approved choice rather
than choosing a new protocol or deriving product policy from another product.

The user-approved Delivery Map revision replaces the initial digest
`3437b86a4263a479037c6a6df793d213fe5eaaf52789704152ec473207fb74d4`:
it requires evidence-preserving cleanup after each build/test batch and lets
the separately authorized legacy-resource-cleanup outcome run independently.
The Design and Plan01 bytes and this capability-retirement scope are unchanged.

## Alternatives and decision

1. Retain both optional features indefinitely. This preserves every existing
   consumer but does not deliver the approved retirement.
2. Disable features or hide menus while retaining the implementations and
   plugin controllers. This leaves callable or advertised surfaces behind and
   is not the target state.
3. Remove framework APIs before changing consumers. This breaks EKO's CI,
   which checks out framework `main`, and ignores the SDK's independent pin.
4. First remove consumer dependencies, then physically retire only the two
   capabilities, with the full pre-retirement version recoverable. **Selected.**

The implementation outcomes are separate: consumer decoupling must be accepted
while the framework still provides the old APIs; framework removal follows.
New framework APIs retain the opposite order: framework first, consumers adopt
afterward. Every mainline merge must leave its then-supported consumers
buildable. No runtime code, feature, lockfile, generated contract, example or CI
matrix changes in this documentation outcome.

## Ownership and preserved capabilities

| Layer | Continues to own | Retirement responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Framework | Generic Agent/Session, revisioned task graph, Subagent, tools/results, cancellation/recovery, HumanLoop, plugin primitives and storage options | Remove the exact A2A/LSP implementations and public/export/registration surfaces after consumer decoupling |
| EKO application | GUI product strategy, workspace/configuration, IM and scheduler coordination, terminal lifecycle and plugin activation | Remove product dependencies and diagnostics/UI/configuration consumers; retain shared execution and background triggers |
| SDK | Protocol, ACP Host adapter, accepted source/kind identities, language projections and resource/stream adapters | Retire only accepted A2A/LSP identities/routes and their consumers; manage its own framework pin |
| Workspace / website | Cross-repository coordination, gitlinks and formal-source mirrors | Synchronize corresponding rules and truthful documentation at each accepted stage |

ACP, MCP, channels, topology, Task/Subagent, tool/result APIs and the framework's
reasonable tool/storage implementation menu remain. EKO continues file-based
persistence and must not enable SQLite; this does not authorize deleting
`echo-state`'s optional SQLite implementation or other reasonable public APIs.
Existing local-personal-product and direct-user-interaction versus automatic
Agent permission boundaries remain in force. No new permission gate, state
authority, task executor or store is introduced by retirement.

## Framework disposition inventory

## Build-batch evidence preservation and cleanup

The user's additional instruction on 2026-10-24 applies to this work and its
implementation follow-ups. It overrides the former rule that kept `target/`
by default and cleaned only at disk/cache thresholds. The framework AGENTS
now carries the same mandatory batch cleanup, concurrency and disk limits.
The approved Delivery Map revision above includes this execution constraint;
the Design and Plan01 inputs remain unchanged.

- After each compilation/test batch actually finishes, preserve the necessary
  logs, real exit status and any Host binary or artifact needed for later
  validation **outside `target/` before cleanup**. Do not delete first and
  subsequently claim the evidence or artifact is still recoverable.
- Confirm that the exact target belongs to this task and has no active
  `cargo`, `rustc`, Host or other artifact reader. Then promptly run
  `cargo clean` for that exact owned target. If it is still in use, defer
  cleanup until the users have finished; do not remove files underneath them.
  Keep worktree targets independent and do not clean another chat's target or
  the primary checkout's cache.
- Run at most two focused Rust builds concurrently; serialize complete build
  and test matrices. Use at most two Cargo jobs per build and disable dev/test
  debug information. Record `df`/`du` disk measurements before and after each
  build batch. Below **5 GiB** available disk space, stop starting new heavy
  builds and let the coordinator resolve the resource constraint.
- For documentation-only or read-only work with no compilation/test batch and
  no task-owned Cargo output, report cleanup as not applicable; do not build
  merely to create something to clean, or clean unrelated directories.

This documentation contribution ran no Cargo compilation or tests and created
no task-owned Cargo output, so no `cargo clean` applies here. The coordinator
owns the separately authorized untracked/uncommitted-file, branch and worktree
maintenance; this clause does not delegate deletion of source, stashes,
recovery refs, worktrees or original evidence to individual contributors.

## Consumer decoupling: frozen build diagnostics

The original documentation contribution above did not remove runtime code.
Plan04 `plan:b6ef1ac6-0745-438d-a3ff-75bb8cdbbcc5`, SHA-256
`336f74dfd00de9b75f84d7101cb9d419f462a6a300bbff416db500f7d77bb070`,
adds a narrow follow-up from framework
`c3b56b4ee8a73565e6a2a621b9a7ddfb644ed3aa`: expose unsupported-build LSP
declarations through the already public generic preparation diagnostics.
No new public type, field, accessor, decoder or state authority is added.

Only the no-LSP build path changes. Successful UTF-8 document freezing keeps
the existing substitution/hash and adds a component/plugin/path Warning that
the build cannot apply LSP. It does not validate YAML or contain EKO product
policy. Invalid UTF-8/read failures stay Error. Wrong filesystem kinds,
metadata errors and broken links must not disappear into generic component
strings or optional NotFound. True absence is not an error, and known
non-regular files are never read as text. Healthy retained components remain
independent and a component error does not invalidate the whole set.

The original prepare/cache owner captures the diagnostic before constructing
the immutable set. Cached sets are returned unchanged; consumers, wiring and
rollback do not probe the package again. The existing feature-on LSP behavior,
document/hash identity inputs and other components remain. Core resolver
public data shapes and generic non-LSP inspection rules are unchanged.

This bridge lets EKO consume `PreparedPluginSet::diagnostics()` instead of
`lsp_document()` or other LSP-specific metadata. Error diagnostics cannot be
recovered from the Warning-only apply-receipt projection, so applications must
consume the complete collection. EKO owns its retirement wording; framework
messages only describe the build capability. EKO switching and acceptance
follow this framework contribution, and physical framework deletion remains
later. The SDK's original framework pin and exact 269/23 retirement boundary
are not changed by the bridge.

Focused red/green, feature-on controls, independent review and normal semantic
validation are required for this contribution. Runtime evidence is recorded
when actually executed; this record does not announce Plan04, both consumers,
the full matrix, main CI or publication complete. Existing examples need no
new API migration because the public preparation interface is unchanged;
website source mirroring belongs to the coordinator.

Local focused evidence for this bridge: the six old-API regression tests first
produced four behavioral failures and two passing controls on the unchanged
production base. The final candidate passed eight default regressions, all 28
prepared-module tests with `mcp`, and all 22 with `mcp,lsp` (58 executions,
zero failures). Both corresponding package-lib Clippy runs with `-D warnings`
exited 0. These use real temporary filesystem inputs, a mock LLM and the
existing local/mock MCP controls; they do not exercise a real language server
or downstream EKO/SDK acceptance. An initial candidate test failure came from
an empty Hook fixture and was corrected to the existing active-rule fixture
without weakening the assertion or changing production behavior. Raw results
and both cleanup receipts remain workspace-only in
`.echo-semantic/local/lsp-frozen-diagnostics/`, outside the cleaned target.
